items.title: CVE-2026-65621: ex_aws_s3 builds x-amz-meta-* request headers by interpolating user-supplied object metadata directly into header names and values without any validation. In ExAws.S3.Utils.build_m
items.summary: ex_aws_s3 builds x-amz-meta-* request headers by interpolating user-supplied object metadata directly into header names and values without any validation. In ExAws.S3.Utils.build_meta_headers/1 (lib/ex_aws/s3/utils.ex), each :meta entry is turned into a header as {"x-amz-meta-#{k}", v} with no check for carriage return (CR), line feed (LF), or other illegal header bytes. Object metadata is routinely derived from end-user input (for example an upload service that lets users attach a comment or label to an object). When such input reaches ExAws.S3.put_object/4 or any other operation accepting the :meta option, a value containing CR/LF is carried unchanged into the outbound header list. If the configured HTTP adapter does not neutralize header values before writing them to the socket, the embedded CRLF starts a new header line, allowing an attacker to inject arbitrary headers into (or split) the HTTP request the library sends to the S3 endpoint. This is an HTTP header (CRLF) injection leading to HTTP request splitting. The practical impact depends on the HTTP adapter, and no authentication is required beyond the ability to influence object metadata. This issue affects ex_aws_s3: from

items.summary: Improper Encoding or Escaping of Output vulnerability in ex-aws ex_aws_ses (ExAws.SES module) allows path injection into Amazon SES V2 request URLs. items.title: CVE-2026-63582: Externally Controlled Reference to a Resource in Another Sphere vulnerability in ex-aws ex_aws_s3 allows an attacker who controls an S3 bucket name to make presigned URLs and presi
items.summary: Externally Controlled Reference to a Resource in Another Sphere vulnerability in ex-aws ex_aws_s3 allows an attacker who controls an S3 bucket name to make presigned URLs and presigned POST forms point at a host of their choice. With virtual_host: true, s3_accelerate: true or bucket_as_host: true, ExAws.S3.presigned_url/5 and ExAws.S3.presigned_post/4 build the URL from the bucket name without checking it. A bucket such as attacker.example/x? turns the URL into https://attacker.example/x?.s3.amazonaws.com..., and the signature is computed for that host. Clients given the URL upload their files to, or download content from, the attacker's host, and every such URL discloses the access key id. With bucket_as_host: true any valid hostname works as the bucket name. This issue affects ex_aws_s3: from 2.0.0 before 2.6.0.

items.title: CVE-2026-63583: ExAws.S3.Utils.build_lifecycle_rule/1 in ex_aws_s3 interpolates caller-supplied lifecycle rule fields (the rule id, filter prefix, tag key and value, storage class, and noncurrent-
items.summary: ExAws.S3.Utils.build_lifecycle_rule/1 in ex_aws_s3 interpolates caller-supplied lifecycle rule fields (the rule id, filter prefix, tag key and value, storage class, and noncurrent-version count) directly into the PutBucketLifecycleConfiguration XML body without escaping XML metacharacters. An application that populates any of these fields from untrusted input (for example a tenant-supplied object tag) lets an attacker break out of the surrounding element and inject arbitrary XML into the request, including an entirely new lifecycle action such as a delete-after-one-day expiration that destroys the bucket's objects. The public entry point ExAws.S3.put_bucket_lifecycle/2 flows directly into this builder. This issue affects ex_aws_s3: from 2.3.0 before 2.6.0.

items.title: CVE-2026-63584: Improper Neutralization of CRLF Sequences ('CRLF Injection') vulnerability in ex-aws ex_aws_s3 allows HTTP header injection via an attacker-controlled copy-source key. ExAws.S3.up
items.summary: Improper Neutralization of CRLF Sequences ('CRLF Injection') vulnerability in ex-aws ex_aws_s3 allows HTTP header injection via an attacker-controlled copy-source key. ExAws.S3.upload_part_copy/8 in lib/ex_aws/s3.ex builds the x-amz-copy-source request header by interpolating the source bucket and object key directly into "/#{src_bucket}/#{src_object}" with no percent-encoding. The sibling function put_object_copy percent-encodes the bucket and each path segment before assembling the same header, but upload_part_copy skips encoding entirely. When the source key is derived from untrusted input, reserved characters (spaces, ?, &, =) pass through verbatim and corrupt the copy-source reference, so the copy targets the wrong object or fails. A key containing \r or \n can split or inject additional headers into the outgoing HTTP request, depending on how the configured HTTP backend serializes headers. Applications that pass a source bucket or object key derived from untrusted input to ExAws.S3.upload_part_copy/8 are affected. Applications that only ever pass trusted, well-formed keys are not affected. This issue affects ex_aws_s3: from 2.0.0 before 2.6.0.

items.title: CVE-2026-63585: ExAws.S3 constructs S3 ACL grant headers (such as x-amz-grant-read and x-amz-grant-full-control) in format_grant_header/1 by interpolating grantee identifiers into a quoted, comma-
items.summary: ExAws.S3 constructs S3 ACL grant headers (such as x-amz-grant-read and x-amz-grant-full-control) in format_grant_header/1 by interpolating grantee identifiers into a quoted, comma-separated list without escaping. Grantee email and id values are wrapped in double quotes and joined with a comma, but double-quote, comma, and CR/LF characters in the value are not neutralized. An application that passes an attacker-influenced grantee value (for example an email address taken from a "share this object" feature) into an ACL grant option (grant_read, grant_write, grant_read_acp, grant_write_acp, or grant_full_control) lets the attacker close the quoted token and inject an additional grantee, such as the attacker's own canonical id or the predefined AllUsers group URI, into the header. S3 then applies the injected grantee, granting an arbitrary principal the same permission (up to full control or public access) in an unintended ACL grantee-injection and privilege-escalation issue. This issue affects ex_aws_s3: from 2.0.0 before 2.6.0.

items.title: CVE-2026-62273: XML Injection vulnerability in ex-aws ex_aws_s3 allows an attacker who controls tag keys or values to inject forged tag entries into S3 object and bucket tagging requests. ExAws.S
items.summary: XML Injection vulnerability in ex-aws ex_aws_s3 allows an attacker who controls tag keys or values to inject forged tag entries into S3 object and bucket tagging requests. ExAws.S3.put_object_tagging/4 and ExAws.S3.put_bucket_tagging/2 in lib/ex_aws/s3.ex build the request body by interpolating tag keys and values directly into and elements via to_string/1, without applying the module's existing escape_xml_string/1 helper (which delete_multiple_objects already uses for object keys). An application that forwards user-supplied data as a tag key or value lets an attacker close the intended element and inject attacker-chosen entries. For example, a tag value of blue owner admin turns one intended tag into two tags on the wire. Because S3 honors tags in access-control conditions (aws:RequestTag, s3:ExistingObjectTag) and cost-allocation reporting, an injected tag can forge an authorization-relevant tag or corrupt the intended tag set. This issue affects ex_aws_s3: from 2.0.2 before 2.6.0.

items.title: CVE-2026-63581: XML Injection vulnerability in ex-aws ex_aws_s3 (ExAws.S3 module) allows an attacker to inject arbitrary XML configuration elements into S3 bucket-configuration request bodies via
items.summary: XML Injection vulnerability in ex-aws ex_aws_s3 (ExAws.S3 module) allows an attacker to inject arbitrary XML configuration elements into S3 bucket-configuration request bodies via unescaped, caller-supplied values. This vulnerability is associated with program files lib/ex_aws/s3.ex and program routines ExAws.S3.put_bucket_logging/2, ExAws.S3.put_bucket_notification/2, ExAws.S3.put_bucket_replication/2, ExAws.S3.put_bucket_website/2. The bucket-configuration body builders construct their XML by interpolating caller-supplied values directly into the request body without escaping, and never route them through the module's own escape_xml_string/1 helper. A value containing XML metacharacters ( , &, quotes) can close the intended element early and open attacker-chosen elements, which the builder's trailing closing tag then closes, keeping the document single-rooted and well-formed. In a multi-tenant application where tenants configure their own bucket settings, an attacker who can influence one of the interpolated field values (for example the logging target, a notification ARN, a replication destination or Account, or a website redirect HostName) can inject arbitrary configuration nod

items.title: CVE-2026-136172: Assimp through 6.0.6 contains a heap out-of-bounds write vulnerability in the OBJ exporter that allows attackers to corrupt memory via NaN vertex components breaking comparator ord
items.summary: Assimp through 6.0.6 contains a heap out-of-bounds write vulnerability in the OBJ exporter that allows attackers to corrupt memory via NaN vertex components breaking comparator ordering. Attackers can supply a crafted PLY file with NaN texture coordinates or vertex colors that, when exported to OBJ in libc++ builds, writes file-controlled data past a heap buffer and crashes the application.

items.title: CVE-2026-136170: Assimp through 6.0.6 contains a use-after-free and double free vulnerability in OpenGEXImporter.cpp because InternReadFile does not reset cached importer state between files. Attac
items.summary: Assimp through 6.0.6 contains a use-after-free and double free vulnerability in OpenGEXImporter.cpp because InternReadFile does not reset cached importer state between files. items.summary: Assimp through 6.0.6 contains a use-after-free vulnerability in BVHLoader.cpp that allows attackers to read freed aiNode objects because the mNodes vector is never cleared between files. items.summary: TypiCMS Core before 17.0.46 contains an insufficiently protected credentials vulnerability that allows authenticated users with "read users" permission to view plaintext api_token values for all users, including superusers, via the GET /api/users endpoint. items.summary: Fider before 0.40.0 contains an account takeover vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to sign in as existing users by linking OAuth identities through unverified email matches. items.summary: Wallabag from 2.0.0-beta.1 before 2.6.16 contains a missing authorization vulnerability that allows authenticated users to annotate other users' entries by referencing global entry IDs. items.summary: vedo through 2026.6.3 contains an insecure deserialization vulnerability that allows attackers to execute code by supplying crafted .npy or .npz files loaded with allow_pickle=True. items.summary: RedVector before 8.1.0 contains a hard-coded credentials vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to execute commands by supplying the default redvector-dev-token bearer token. items.summary: Cockpit CMS through 2.14.1 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows authenticated users with content create or update permission to inject script via unescaped linked item _id values. items.title: CVE-2026-136131: hping3 through commit 3547c76 contains an out-of-bounds write vulnerability in display_ipopt() that allows remote attackers to overflow the static 40-byte old_rr buffer via a craft
items.summary: hping3 through commit 3547c76 contains an out-of-bounds write vulnerability in display_ipopt() that allows remote attackers to overflow the static 40-byte old_rr buffer via a crafted IP Record Route option. items.title: CVE-2026-136132: Pangolin before 1.21.0 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability in isPathAllowed() in server/lib/pathMatch.ts that splits paths on literal slashes without percent-decoding o
items.summary: Pangolin before 1.21.0 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability in isPathAllowed() in server/lib/pathMatch.ts that splits paths on literal slashes without percent-decoding or resolving dot segments. Unauthenticated remote attackers can send paths with encoded slashes and dot segments to match public bypass rules while backends serve protected paths.

items.title: CVE-2026-136133: NocoDB before 2026.10.2 contains a denial of service vulnerability in passwordForgot() that allows unauthenticated attackers to revoke a user's sessions by requesting a password re
items.summary: NocoDB before 2026.10.2 contains a denial of service vulnerability in passwordForgot() that allows unauthenticated attackers to revoke a user's sessions by requesting a password reset. Attackers who know a user's email can repeatedly request resets to sign out users, including super-admins, and permanently destroy their OAuth and MCP application authorizations.

items.title: CVE-2026-136155: In Valkey 9.1.0 and 9.1.1, the Lua script debugger builds its command table once and caches it with a pointer to the Lua interpreter state that was current at the time. SCRIPT FLUS
items.summary: In Valkey 9.1.0 and 9.1.1, the Lua script debugger builds its command table once and caches it with a pointer to the Lua interpreter state that was current at the time. SCRIPT FLUSH ASYNC recreates the scripting engine and frees the previous interpreter state without invalidating that cache, so the next debugger command dereferences freed memory. An authenticated user who can run scripting commands can use this to reliably crash the server, and by reclaiming the freed heap chunk with attacker-controlled bytes can escalate it to control of an indirect call, which may lead to remote code execution. The fix also addresses a second use-after-free in ldbLogStackValue. Valkey 8.0.x and 8.1.x use the previous debugger and are not affected.

items.title: CVE-2026-136156: In Valkey before 7.2.15, 8.0.x before 8.0.12, 8.1.x before 8.1.11, 9.0.x before 9.0.7, 9.1.x before 9.1.3 and 9.2.0-rc1, running in cluster mode, clusterCreatePublishMsgBlock compu
items.summary: In Valkey before 7.2.15, 8.0.x before 8.0.12, 8.1.x before 8.1.11, 9.0.x before 9.0.7, 9.1.x before 9.1.3 and 9.2.0-rc1, running in cluster mode, clusterCreatePublishMsgBlock computes the length of the cluster bus message for a PUBLISH or SPUBLISH as a size_t but passes it to createClusterMsgSendBlock as a uint32_t. When the channel and message together exceed 4 GiB, the length is truncated, a buffer far smaller than the message is allocated, and the full channel and message are then copied into it. An authenticated user who can publish, for example by building the arguments in a script, can overflow the heap with attacker-controlled bytes. This reliably crashes the server and may lead to remote code execution. Servers that do not run in cluster mode are not affected.

items.title: CVE-2026-136157: In Valkey 8.0.x before 8.0.11, 8.1.x before 8.1.10, 9.0.x before 9.0.6 and 9.1.x before 9.1.2, the RDMA transport's pending-data handler walks its connection list with an iterator
items.summary: In Valkey 8.0.x before 8.0.11, 8.1.x before 8.1.10, 9.0.x before 9.0.6 and 9.1.x before 9.1.2, the RDMA transport's pending-data handler walks its connection list with an iterator that caches the next entry. A command processed from inside that loop, such as CLIENT KILL, can synchronously free another client's connection, and closing an RDMA connection did not remove it from the pending list, so the handler then uses freed memory. An authenticated user can use this to reliably crash the server, and the freed heap chunk can be reclaimed with attacker-influenced bytes. Only servers built with RDMA support (USE_RDMA) and configured with an RDMA listener are affected.

items.title: CVE-2026-136158: In Valkey JSON 1.0.0 through 1.0.2, a recursive JSONPath expression such as $..* returns both an array and elements nested inside it. The size-changing mutators (JSON.ARRAPPEND, JS
items.summary: In Valkey JSON 1.0.0 through 1.0.2, a recursive JSONPath expression such as $..* returns both an array and elements nested inside it. The size-changing mutators (JSON.ARRAPPEND, JSON.ARRINSERT, JSON.ARRPOP, JSON.ARRTRIM and JSON.CLEAR) process the ancestor first, which can reallocate its element buffer and free the old storage while the descendant entries in the result set still point into it; the module then writes through those dangling pointers. An authenticated user who can run these commands can use this to reliably crash the server, and it has been developed into remote code execution as the user the server runs as. Servers that do not load the JSON module, including through valkey-bundle, are not affected.

items.title: CVE-2026-135908: Rapid7 Metasploit Framework versions prior to 6.5.10 are vulnerable to an uncontrolled resource consumption issue in Rex::Proto::Http::Request#normalize!. A remote, unauthenticated
items.summary: Rapid7 Metasploit Framework versions prior to 6.5.10 are vulnerable to an uncontrolled resource consumption issue in Rex::Proto::Http::Request#normalize!. A remote, unauthenticated attacker can send an HTTP request with a deeply nested path that triggers repeated rescans of the request target, causing quadratic CPU consumption and temporarily degrading the availability of any affected HTTP listener. The issue is fixed in Metasploit Framework 6.5.10

items.title: CVE-2026-133555: Use of Externally-Controlled Input to Select Classes or Code ('Unsafe Reflection') vulnerability in elixir-ecto db_connection allows an attacker to execute arbitrary code via a for
items.summary: Use of Externally-Controlled Input to Select Classes or Code ('Unsafe Reflection') vulnerability in elixir-ecto db_connection allows an attacker to execute arbitrary code via a forged DBConnection.Stream or DBConnection.PrepareStream struct. The Enumerable implementations of both structs in lib/db_connection.ex run with the options stored in the struct. The :log option accepts a {module, function, arguments} tuple, which DBConnection applies. When code enumerates a forged struct, DBConnection calls the chosen function. This issue is not exploitable in db_connection alone. It is, in theory, a vulnerability of the downstream component. The root cause is a component that decodes untrusted input with :erlang.binary_to_term/2 and does not restrict which terms the result contains. The :safe option does not reject structs, and these structs contain only plain terms. Structs of other libraries can possibly lead to the same result, so a component that decodes untrusted terms stays at risk independently of db_connection. This record exists because the struct was used in attacks on such components. This issue affects db_connection: from 1.1.0 before 2.10.3.

items.title: CVE-2026-131902: XML Injection vulnerability in ex-aws ex_aws_s3 allows an attacker who controls an object version id passed to ExAws.S3.delete_multiple_objects/3 to add objects to the batch delete
items.summary: XML Injection vulnerability in ex-aws ex_aws_s3 allows an attacker who controls an object version id passed to ExAws.S3.delete_multiple_objects/3 to add objects to the batch delete. delete_multiple_objects/3 in lib/ex_aws/s3.ex builds the request body by placing each object's version between tags without XML escaping. A version such as v1 important-file x v2 closes the caller's object and opens new ones, so S3 deletes objects the application never listed, including other users' objects in the same bucket. This issue affects ex_aws_s3: from 2.0.0 before 2.6.0.

items.title: CVE-2026-130411: Deserialization of Untrusted Data vulnerability in woylie flop allows a remote attacker to execute code on the server via a crafted pagination cursor. Flop.Cursor.decode/2 in lib/
items.summary: Deserialization of Untrusted Data vulnerability in woylie flop allows a remote attacker to execute code on the server via a crafted pagination cursor. Flop.Cursor.decode/2 in lib/flop/cursor.ex decodes the after and before parameters with :erlang.binary_to_term/2 in :safe mode. Its check rejects functions, PIDs, ports and references, but it accepts maps, and therefore structs of any module. Flop passes the decoded values to Ecto as query parameters. A cursor value that nests an Ecto.Query.DynamicExpr struct with a DBConnection.Stream struct as its binding fails the Ecto cast. Ecto then inspects the value for the error message, the Inspect implementation enumerates the stream, and DBConnection calls the module, function and arguments in the :log option of the stream. This issue affects flop: from 0.8.0 before 0.26.7, from 0.27.0 before 0.27.3, from 0.28.0 before 0.28.1, and from 0.29.0 before 0.29.2.

items.title: CVE-2026-124286: Improper Verification of Cryptographic Signature vulnerability in Erlang OTP ssl (ssl_handshake module) allows an on-path attacker to impersonate any server to a TLS 1.2 or DTLS cl
items.summary: Improper Verification of Cryptographic Signature vulnerability in Erlang OTP ssl (ssl_handshake module) allows an on-path attacker to impersonate any server to a TLS 1.2 or DTLS client. When a server sends no Certificate message and a ServerKeyExchange without a signature, ssl_handshake:decode_server_key/3 reports the signature algorithm as anon, and ssl_handshake:verify_signature/5 returns true for anon without a public key. The client does not require a certificate for a certificate-authenticated key exchange, so the handshake completes for the ecdhe_rsa, ecdhe_ecdsa, dhe_rsa and dhe_dss key exchanges with a cipher suite the client offered. Certificate path validation, verify_fun and the hostname check do not run, and ssl:connect/3 returns {ok, Socket} with {verify, verify_peer} set. The TLS 1.3 client is not affected. This issue affects OTP from OTP 17.0 before OTP 27.3.4.14, OTP 28.5.0.9, and OTP 29.0.3, corresponding to ssl from 5.3.4 before 11.2.12.10, 11.6.0.8, and 11.7.3.

items.title: CVE-2026-119443: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference vulnerability in xmerl_scan in Erlang OTP xmerl allows an attacker to exhaust the memory of the Erlang VM via an XML document
items.summary: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference vulnerability in xmerl_scan in Erlang OTP xmerl allows an attacker to exhaust the memory of the Erlang VM via an XML document that names an external DTD. With default options, xmerl_scan:string/1,2 and xmerl_scan:file/1,2 fetch and parse the external DTD named in a declaration. fetch_DTD/2 in lib/xmerl/src/xmerl_scan.erl passes every system identifier to the default fetch function, which maps file: and absolute URIs to local paths, and int_file_decl/3 then reads the whole file with file:read_file/1. This happens whether or not validation is enabled, and the allow_entities option, which is false by default since OTP 27, only governs declarations and does not stop the fetch. A document naming file:///dev/zero makes the node read without bound until the operating system kills it for lack of memory, and the parse never returns. This issue affects OTP from OTP 17.0 before OTP 27.3.4.20, OTP 28.5.0.9, and OTP 29.1.3, corresponding to xmerl from 1.3.7 before 2.1.3.4, 2.1.9.1, and 2.2.1. Whether OTP before OTP 17.0, corresponding to xmerl before 1.3.7, is affected is unknown.

items.title: CVE-2026-120961: Out-of-bounds Read vulnerability in the external term format decoder in Erlang OTP erts allows an attacker who controls the input to binary_to_term/1,2 to read memory after the inp
items.summary: Out-of-bounds Read vulnerability in the external term format decoder in Erlang OTP erts allows an attacker who controls the input to binary_to_term/1,2 to read memory after the input, and to change one byte there, via a FLOAT_EXT term without a terminating zero byte. decoded_size in erts/emulator/beam/external.c checks only that the 31 bytes of the FLOAT_EXT field are present. dec_term then passes the field to sys_chars_to_double, which scans to a NUL byte without a length limit. When the field has no NUL, the scan continues into the bytes after the field, and those bytes change the decoded float. When the radix character is found after the field and strtod does not accept it, sys_chars_to_double overwrites that byte (a , becomes a .). The VM can fault if the scan reaches an unmapped page. The safe option does not prevent this. enif_binary_to_term() and the distribution protocol reach the same decoder, and distribution is assumed to run on trusted networks only. The write is limited to the one radix byte. No arbitrary write or code execution was shown. This issue affects OTP from OTP 17.0 before OTP 27.3.4.20, OTP 28.5.0.9, and OTP 29.1.3, corresponding to erts from 6.0 before 15.2

items.title: CVE-2026-117642: Uncontrolled Recursion vulnerability in the external term format decoder in Erlang OTP erts allows an attacker who controls the input to binary_to_term/1,2 to abort the Erlang VM v
items.summary: Uncontrolled Recursion vulnerability in the external term format decoder in Erlang OTP erts allows an attacker who controls the input to binary_to_term/1,2 to abort the Erlang VM via a fun term with funs nested in its integer fields. dec_term in erts/emulator/beam/external.c decodes terms iteratively, except for the OldIndex and OldUniq fields of NEW_FUN_EXT and the Arity field of EXPORT_EXT. For these fields it calls itself, and it checks that the result is a small integer only after the call returns. An input that places another fun in such a field, nested to sufficient depth, recurses once per level, exhausts the stack of the scheduler thread and crashes the VM. The input must be large enough to reach that depth. The abort takes down every process on the node. Supervision, try/catch and the safe option do not prevent it. enif_binary_to_term() and the distribution protocol reach the same decoder, and distribution is assumed to run on trusted networks only. This issue affects OTP from OTP 17.0 before OTP 27.3.4.20, OTP 28.5.0.9, and OTP 29.1.3, corresponding to erts from 6.0 before 15.2.7.15, 16.4.0.8, and 17.1.2. Whether OTP before OTP 17.0, corresponding to erts before 6.0, is a

items.title: CVE-2026-116293: Out-of-bounds Write vulnerability in the external term format decoder in Erlang OTP erts allows an attacker who controls the input to binary_to_term/1,2 to abort the Erlang VM via
items.summary: Out-of-bounds Write vulnerability in the external term format decoder in Erlang OTP erts allows an attacker who controls the input to binary_to_term/1,2 to abort the Erlang VM via a NEWER_REFERENCE_EXT term with a zero-length ID. decoded_size in erts/emulator/beam/external.c accepts a reference whose 16-bit Len field is zero, but dec_term always reads one ID word. dec_term then runs 4 bytes ahead of the position that decoded_size validated. It decodes the bytes that follow as terms that were never sized, and writes past the reserved process heap. The abort takes down every process on the node. Supervision, try/catch and the safe option do not prevent it. enif_binary_to_term() and the distribution protocol reach the same decoder, and distribution is assumed to run on trusted networks only. NEW_REFERENCE_EXT also accepts a zero length, but its range check on the first ID word rejects the shifted input. On 32-bit builds, a zero-length reference of either type at the end of the input, followed by trailing bytes, can write one word past the reserved heap. This issue affects OTP from OTP 17.0 before OTP 27.3.4.20, OTP 28.5.0.9, and OTP 29.1.3, corresponding to erts from 6.0 before 15.2.7

items.title: CVE-2026-116295: Improper Neutralization of CRLF Sequences in HTTP Headers ('HTTP Request/Response Splitting') vulnerability in Erlang OTP inets (httpc module) allows HTTP Request Splitting. httpc
items.summary: Improper Neutralization of CRLF Sequences in HTTP Headers ('HTTP Request/Response Splitting') vulnerability in Erlang OTP inets (httpc module) allows HTTP Request Splitting. httpc writes request header names and values to the wire without neutralizing CR, LF or NUL characters. On the default path http_request:mk_key_value_str/2, and with the headers_as_is option httpc_request:http_headers/2, build each header line by plain concatenation of the name, ": ", the value and CRLF. A CR/LF in a name or value ends the header line early. An attacker who controls data that an application puts into a header passed to httpc:request/4,5 can add or override request headers, or append a second request on the same connection. Applications that pass only constant or validated header names and values are not affected. The request line is not affected, because uri_string rejects URLs that contain raw CR/LF. This issue affects OTP from OTP 17.0 before OTP 27.3.4.20, OTP 28.5.0.9, and OTP 29.1.3, corresponding to inets from 5.10 before 9.3.2.9, 9.6.2.5, and 9.8.2. Whether OTP before OTP 17.0, corresponding to inets before 5.10, is affected is unknown.

items.title: CVE-2026-116382: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling vulnerability in Erlang OTP inets (httpd_script_env module) allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to exhaust the atom table
items.summary: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling vulnerability in Erlang OTP inets (httpd_script_env module) allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to exhaust the atom table of an httpd server that serves ESI scripts. When mod_esi builds the environment for an ESI callback, httpd_script_env:http_env_element/3 checks that a request header name already exists as an atom, then creates the atom http_ with list_to_atom/1. Atoms are never garbage collected, and each new atom passes the existence check on a later request. So a header named node creates http_node, a header named http_node creates http_http_node, and so on. A stream of requests to any ESI URL grows the atom table until it reaches its limit (+t), and then the whole Erlang VM aborts, together with every application on the node. This issue affects OTP from OTP 17.0 before OTP 27.3.4.20, OTP 28.5.0.9, and OTP 29.1.3, corresponding to inets from 5.10 before 9.3.2.9, 9.6.2.5, and 9.8.2. Whether OTP before OTP 17.0, corresponding to inets before 5.10, is affected is unknown.

items.title: CVE-2026-116225: Improper Validation of Specified Quantity in Input vulnerability in the BER decoder in Erlang/OTP snmp allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to exhaust CPU via an SNMP message
items.summary: Improper Validation of Specified Quantity in Input vulnerability in the BER decoder in Erlang/OTP snmp allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to exhaust CPU via an SNMP message that contains an OBJECT IDENTIFIER with a very long sub-identifier. snmp_pdus:dec_oid_element/3 does not limit the number of base-128 octets in a sub-identifier, and snmp_pdus:dec_oid_elements/3 does not limit the number of sub-identifiers, so one sub-identifier can span the whole datagram. When the value exceeds the native integer size, each further octet copies a growing bignum, and decoding time grows quadratically with the sub-identifier length. The agent and the manager decode OIDs before they check community strings or SNMPv3 credentials, inside the single network interface process (snmpa_net_if or snmpm_net_if). That process does not read the next datagram until decoding completes. This issue affects OTP from OTP 17.0 before OTP 27.3.4.20, OTP 28.5.0.9, and OTP 29.1.3, corresponding to snmp from 4.25.1 before 5.18.2.3, 5.20.2.4, and 5.20.7. Whether OTP before OTP 17.0, corresponding to snmp before 4.25.1, is affected is unknown.

items.title: CVE-2026-130822: In Valkey before 7.2.16, 8.0.x before 8.0.13, 8.1.x before 8.1.12, 9.0.x before 9.0.8, 9.1.x before 9.1.4 and 9.2.0 release candidates, when client eviction is enabled (maxmemory-c
items.summary: In Valkey before 7.2.16, 8.0.x before 8.0.13, 8.1.x before 8.1.12, 9.0.x before 9.0.8, 9.1.x before 9.1.4 and 9.2.0 release candidates, when client eviction is enabled (maxmemory-clients is not 0), an authenticated user who can write to a key that other clients are blocked on (for example with BLPOP, BLMPOP, BZPOPMIN or XREAD BLOCK) can trigger a use-after-free. While the clients blocked on that key are served, evictClients() can select and free the client whose command made the key ready, although that command is still executing, and the server then keeps using the freed client. The blocked clients do not have to belong to the attacker. The result is a reliable crash of the server process. Servers with the default maxmemory-clients 0 are not affected.

items.title: CVE-2026-120299: Improper Input Validation vulnerability in ash-project ash allows an attacker to bypass the input validation of the field types of a :keyword attribute or argument. Ash.Type.Keywo
items.summary: Improper Input Validation vulnerability in ash-project ash allows an attacker to bypass the input validation of the field types of a :keyword attribute or argument. Ash.Type.Keyword.cast_input/2 in lib/ash/type/keyword.ex converts a map input to a keyword list in try_map_to_keyword/2, which casts each declared field with Ash.Type.cast_stored/3. That function is meant for trusted values read back from the data layer, so client input skips the cast_input/2 of each field type. apply_constraints/2 casts the result again with cast_input/2, but most types accept a value of their own type unchanged. An embedded resource field is built without its create action, so its validations and changes do not run and its non-public attributes can be set. A :function field accepts a capture string such as &Mod.fun/1, and a :term field decodes Erlang external term format. This issue affects ash: from 3.24.0 before 3.38.1.

items.title: CVE-2026-129514: Deserialization of Untrusted Data vulnerability in the application/vnd.hex+erlang request body parser in hexpm hexpm allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to execute operating
items.summary: Deserialization of Untrusted Data vulnerability in the application/vnd.hex+erlang request body parser in hexpm hexpm allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to execute operating system commands via a crafted Erlang external term format request body. This vulnerability was actively exploited against the hex.pm service on 2026-11-23. HexpmWeb.ErlangFormat.decode/1 in lib/hexpm_web/erlang_format.ex decodes the body with Plug.Crypto.non_executable_binary_to_term/2, which accepts maps that have a __struct__ key. HexpmWeb.PlugParser.parse/5 returns the decoded term as the request params. The parser runs in the endpoint before routing and authentication, so a POST to any route reaches it. Elixir dispatches protocols on the __struct__ key, so the client selects which Inspect and Enumerable implementations run when error reporting inspects the params. A chain through Ecto.Query.DynamicExpr and DBConnection.Stream reaches an apply/3 call on a {module, function, args} tuple taken from the request body. This issue affects hex.pm: from 2016-02-23 before 2026-11-23; hexpm/hexpm: from ab1bbcef7cc8395d1056d3b1aa6a174353492d59 before 379b0a29bcc95164249f38ad7d772a37a8ff9533.

items.title: CVE-2026-62271: Use of RSA Algorithm without OAEP vulnerability in ex-aws ex_aws_kms (ExAws.KMS module) causes callers who import external key material to wrap their secret KMS key material with t
items.summary: Use of RSA Algorithm without OAEP vulnerability in ex-aws ex_aws_kms (ExAws.KMS module) causes callers who import external key material to wrap their secret KMS key material with the deprecated PKCS#1 v1.5 padding scheme by default. This vulnerability is associated with program file lib/ex_aws/kms.ex and program routine ExAws.KMS.get_parameters_for_import/3. ExAws.KMS.get_parameters_for_import/3 defaults its wrapping_algorithm argument to "RSAES_PKCS1_V1_5". AWS KMS returns this value as the WrappingAlgorithm for the import operation, and it dictates the RSA padding scheme the caller uses to wrap (RSA-encrypt) their secret key material before calling ImportKeyMaterial. AWS KMS also supports the stronger RSAES_OAEP_SHA_1 and RSAES_OAEP_SHA_256 schemes. By defaulting to RSAES_PKCS1_V1_5, the library steers callers who do not explicitly override the argument toward the weakest of the three. PKCS#1 v1.5 encryption padding is susceptible to Bleichenbacher adaptive chosen-ciphertext (padding oracle) attacks, which can recover the wrapped plaintext without the private key given an oracle that reveals whether a decrypted value was validly padded. items.title: CVE-2026-62270: Improper Validation of Specified Type of Input in ExAws.Dynamo.Encoder.encode/2 in ex_aws_dynamo allows an attacker who controls map data passed into a DynamoDB call to choose the
items.summary: Improper Validation of Specified Type of Input in ExAws.Dynamo.Encoder.encode/2 in ex_aws_dynamo allows an attacker who controls map data passed into a DynamoDB call to choose the raw stored DynamoDB AttributeValue. The encode/2 function in lib/ex_aws/dynamo/encoder.ex has one clause per DynamoDB type descriptor ("S", "N", "B", "BOOL", "M", "L", "NS", "SS", "BS", "NULL") that treats any map merely containing such a key as already encoded and returns it verbatim, bypassing the ExAws.Dynamo.Encodable protocol. The match is on the presence of the key alone, so no check is made that the value is well formed for the claimed type, and extra keys and arbitrary nested content survive untouched. An application that threads user-influenced map data (a decoded JSON body, a nested attribute, or an expression_attribute_values entry) into a Dynamo write or query therefore lets the user, rather than the application, decide the stored attribute's declared type, its bytes, and its structure. This type confusion breaks round-trip integrity and enables silent persistent data corruption, injection of attributes and raw binaries the schema never sanctioned, subversion of application authorization check

items.title: CVE-2026-133769: Cva::apply() converted the values of variants, default variants and compound variants with (array). These values come from the arguments of html_cva(). A sandboxed template could t
items.summary: Cva::apply() converted the values of variants, default variants and compound variants with (array). These values come from the arguments of html_cva(). A sandboxed template could therefore pass any object of its context, and print the private and protected properties of that object: {{ html_cva('base', {c: {p: user}}).apply({c: 'p'}) }} Variant maps that are ArrayAccess objects were also read with a key that the template chooses, without the property check of the sandbox. The template then printed the offsets that the object returned. Applications are affected when the sandbox allows the html_cva function and the apply method of Twig\Extra\Html\Cva. A value that isn't an array is now treated as a single item, so objects are dropped and never match a variant. Variant maps are also only used when they're arrays.

items.title: CVE-2026-133770: The sandbox allows every method of Twig\Markup objects, including their public constructor. A sandboxed template can therefore call __construct() on any Markup object that it reach
items.summary: The sandbox allows every method of Twig\Markup objects, including their public constructor. A sandboxed template can therefore call __construct() on any Markup object that it reaches, and replace its content: {% do banner.__construct(' alert(1) ', 'UTF-8') %} A template gains nothing by rewriting its own output. The impact is on the Markup objects that come from the application and are also rendered elsewhere, like a global in a long-running worker. Their new content then ends up in trusted pages that aren't sandboxed. The sandbox no longer allows calling the constructor of Markup objects.

items.title: CVE-2026-133771: The escaper considered x.attr, x['key'] and x.method() safe whenever {% import ... as x %} appeared anywhere in the template. Macro calls haven't needed this rule since Twig 3.0. I
items.summary: The escaper considered x.attr, x['key'] and x.method() safe whenever {% import ... as x %} appeared anywhere in the template. Macro calls haven't needed this rule since Twig 3.0. It only matched ordinary variables that have the name of an alias imported in another block or macro, and printed them without escaping: {% block header %}{% import _self as item %}{{ item.hello() }}{% endblock %} {% block content %}{% for item in items %}{{ item.body }}{% endfor %}{% endblock %} Here, item.body is printed raw. This leads to XSS when the value comes from an attacker. The same happens with an import in a macro and an argument of the same name in another macro. It also happens with a template-level import placed after the block that uses the name. The rule is removed. Macro calls through an alias are still considered safe.

items.title: CVE-2026-133772: The guard tag compiles only one of its branches, depending on whether a callable exists. The other branch was still parsed, though. The extends, use, macro and block tags in it reg
items.summary: The guard tag compiles only one of its branches, depending on whether a callable exists. The other branch was still parsed, though. The extends, use, macro and block tags in it registered their effects on the template. The sandbox doesn't see these tags, since that branch isn't compiled. A sandboxed template allowed to use guard could therefore extend a template, import blocks and define macros, while the policy doesn't allow these tags: {% guard filter upper %}{% else %}{% extends "parent.html" %}{% endguard %} The templates reached this way come from the loader of the sandbox, and they are sandboxed too. What the branch that isn't selected registers on the parser is now discarded.

items.title: CVE-2026-133773: The html_to_markdown filter of twig/markdown-extra keeps an HtmlConverter for each distinct mapping of options it receives. They're kept in a static array, with no size limit and n
items.summary: The html_to_markdown filter of twig/markdown-extra keeps an HtmlConverter for each distinct mapping of options it receives. They're kept in a static array, with no size limit and no eviction. The options are an argument of the filter. A template that passes options taken from the input, or a sandboxed template, can therefore make this cache grow without limit. The cache outlives the environment, so it fills the memory of long-running workers. The cache now keeps at most 100 converters, like the formatter caches of IntlExtension.

items.title: CVE-2026-133763: The sandbox checks that a template may call toString() on an object before converting it to a string. For an object, the is true test evaluates to the object itself, and that resul
items.summary: The sandbox checks that a template may call toString() on an object before converting it to a string. For an object, the is true test evaluates to the object itself, and that result wasn't checked. A sandboxed template could therefore print an object through a denied toString() method: {{ obj is true }} The same applies when the result is concatenated or passed to a filter. No tag needs to be allowed. A test in a boolean context, like {% if obj is true %}, isn't affected, since it doesn't convert the object to a string. The sandbox now checks the result of tests like the result of filters and functions.

items.title: CVE-2026-133764: The sandbox checks that a template may call toString() on an object before converting it to a string. It didn't check the input of tests. The PHP callable of a test may convert thi
items.summary: The sandbox checks that a template may call toString() on an object before converting it to a string. It didn't check the input of tests. The PHP callable of a test may convert this input to a string, for example when its parameter is typed as string. PHP then calls toString() on an object without the sandbox checking it first: {{ obj is upperish }} Applications are affected when they register such a test and allow it in the sandbox. No built-in test is affected. The sandbox now checks the input of tests like the input of filters. The built-in tests that never convert their input to a string still skip the check.

items.title: CVE-2026-133765: The sandbox checks that a template may call toString() on an object before converting it to a string. Since Twig 3.23.0, assignments like x = obj, and the destructuring forms [a] =
items.summary: The sandbox checks that a template may call toString() on an object before converting it to a string. Since Twig 3.23.0, assignments like x = obj, and the destructuring forms [a] = list and {a} = obj, evaluate to the value that they assign. The sandbox didn't check that value, so a sandboxed template could call a denied toString() method: {{ (x = obj) }} {{ ({secret: s} = obj)|join }} No tag needs to be allowed. The sandbox now checks the result of assignments like the result of filters and functions. {% do x = obj %} and {% if (x = obj) %} still work, since they don't convert the value to a string.

items.title: CVE-2026-133766: Since Twig 3.28.0, the sandbox skips the toString() check of an argument whose PHP parameter can't hold a string, like an int. A spread argument was mapped to a single parameter, a
items.summary: Since Twig 3.28.0, the sandbox skips the toString() check of an argument whose PHP parameter can't hold a string, like an int. A spread argument was mapped to a single parameter, although it fills every parameter from its position on. A sandboxed template could therefore call a denied toString() method: {{ tag(...[1, obj]) }} Here, the first parameter of tag() is an int, and a later one accepts strings. Applications are affected when they allow such a function, filter or test in the sandbox. No built-in callable is affected. A spread argument is now checked unless every parameter that it can fill has a safe type.

items.title: CVE-2026-133767: When the parent of an embed tag was an expression other than a string or a variable, the sandbox didn't see that expression. The functions, filters and tests of the expression were
items.summary: When the parent of an embed tag was an expression other than a string or a variable, the sandbox didn't see that expression. The functions, filters and tests of the expression weren't checked against the policy, and neither were its conversions to strings. A sandboxed template allowed to use embed could therefore call any function, filter or test, and any __toString() method: {% embed 'leak_' ~ app_secret() %}{% endembed %} Method calls and property reads were not affected, since they're checked at runtime. The sandbox now checks the parent expression of embed like any other expression of the template.

items.title: CVE-2026-133768: The join filter converted a value that isn't iterable with (array) $value. For an object, that gives every property, including the private and protected ones. A sandboxed template
items.summary: The join filter converted a value that isn't iterable with (array) $value. For an object, that gives every property, including the private and protected ones. A sandboxed template allowed to use join could therefore print properties that the policy denies, and that templates can't read otherwise: {{ user|join(',') }} A value that isn't iterable is now joined as a single item. A Stringable object prints its checked string, and other objects throw, as with the first and last filters.

items.title: CVE-2026-120720: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) vulnerability in ex-aws ex_aws allows an attacker who controls an S3 bucket name to send the application's signed S3 requests to a host of their
items.summary: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) vulnerability in ex-aws ex_aws allows an attacker who controls an S3 bucket name to send the application's signed S3 requests to a host of their choice. With virtual_host: true, ExAws.Operation.S3.add_bucket_to_path/2 in lib/ex_aws/operation/s3.ex builds the request hostname from the bucket name and the configured host without checking the bucket name. A bucket such as attacker.example/x? turns the request URL into https://attacker.example/x?.s3.amazonaws.com/key, so the request is signed for and sent to attacker.example. The attacker receives upload bodies, the access key id and request signature, and any STS session token, and controls the response the application parses. With bucket_as_host: true the bucket is the whole hostname, so any valid hostname redirects the request. This issue affects ex_aws: from 2.1.7 before 2.8.0.

items.summary: Improper Encoding or Escaping of Output vulnerability in ex_aws (S3 request URL construction). This vulnerability is associated with program files lib/ex_aws/request/url.ex and program routines ExAws.Request.Url.build/2, ExAws.Request.Url.sanitize/2 and ExAws.Request.Url.get_path/2. ex_aws does not percent-encode reserved characters in S3 object keys when it assembles the request URL. items.summary: Issue summary: A QUIC peer that sends many small out-of-order STREAM fragments while withholding the first byte of the stream may cause OpenSSL to buffer a large number of reassembly nodes occupying much larger memory than the actual data sent. Impact summary: A remote peer can pin large amounts of memory on a server that accepts incoming QUIC streams, potentially exhausting memory and causing Denial of Service. A peer that opens a stream and sends many one-byte fragments at increasing offsets, while withholding the first byte, makes the receiver retain one node per fragment without delivering any data. Only applications that accept incoming streams are exposed. With the default policy, which rejects peer-initiated streams, the stream is torn down before state accumulates. items.title: CVE-2026-59697: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) vulnerability in ex_aws (instance metadata token provider). This vulnerability is associated with program files lib/ex_aws/instance_meta_token_p
items.summary: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) vulnerability in ex_aws (instance metadata token provider). This vulnerability is associated with program files lib/ex_aws/instance_meta_token_provider.ex and program routines ExAws.InstanceMetaTokenProvider.request_token/1 and ExAws.InstanceMetaTokenProvider.get/1. ex_aws requests its IMDSv2 session token from the link-local metadata endpoint (http://169.254.169.254/latest/api/token) with HTTP redirect following enabled. Because the token request follows 3xx redirects and does not restrict the redirect target to the link-local range, an attacker who can influence the response to the metadata request (for example an on-segment neighbor spoofing the link-local address) can answer with a redirect to an arbitrary host. The library follows the redirect and accepts the arbitrary host's response body as the IMDSv2 session token, caching it and sending it as the x-aws-ec2-metadata-token header on every subsequent metadata and credential request. This issue affects ex_aws: from 2.3.0 before 2.8.0.

items.title: CVE-2026-59698: Relative path traversal in ex_aws allows an attacker who controls an S3 object key to escape the intended bucket or key prefix. When ex_aws builds a path-style S3 request, ExAws.O
items.summary: Relative path traversal in ex_aws allows an attacker who controls an S3 object key to escape the intended bucket or key prefix. Because the bucket is the first segment of the combined string, a leading ../ in the object key pops the bucket off the path. The same mechanism collapses ../ within a key, defeating any isolation an application enforces by prepending a trusted prefix. Only the default path-style configuration is affected; requests built with virtual_host: true do not run this normalization. items.title: CVE-2026-82444: Description `CookieConverter.getCookies` decides which stored cookies to attach to an outbound request. The applicability check is nested inside a test for the presence of a `Doma
items.summary: Description `CookieConverter.getCookies` decides which stored cookies to attach to an outbound request. The applicability check is nested inside a test for the presence of a `Domain` attribute, so a cookie without one, which is the ordinary form of a session cookie, skips scoping entirely and is returned for whatever target URL was passed. RFC 6265 requires the opposite: a cookie with no `Domain` attribute is host-only and belongs to the host that set it. Two further defects sit in the same method. The domain comparison has no notion of a registrable domain, so a `Domain` value of `com` matches every host under it, and the comparison returns true when it throws, so a failure to evaluate the check admits the cookie. Neither the converter nor `MetadataTransfer`, which carries the stored cookie to outlinks, ever considers the host that issued it. Cookie handling is opt-in: it requires `http.use.cookies` to be set to true, which is not the default, and the cookie key to be listed in `metadata.transfer`. The documented recipe does not work as written, because the `metadata.transfer` example in the internals documentation names `set-cookie` while the key present in metadata is `protocol.

items.summary: Description The SQL status backend serialises per-URL metadata into a single column by concatenating a tabulation, the key, an equals sign and the value, with no escaping. On read-back the string is split on the same two characters, so the round trip is not injective: a value that contains a tabulation returns as one or more additional keys that were never written. Values on that path are supplied by crawled servers. `FetcherBolt` records the raw `Location` header of a redirect as `_redirTo`, and `_redirTo` is part of the default `metadata.persist` set, so a redirect whose `Location` contains a tabulation followed by `key=value` pairs introduces those keys into the crawler's own control metadata on the next scheduling cycle. items.title: CVE-2026-82446: Description When StormCrawler fetches a host's `/robots.txt` and receives a redirect, `HttpRobotRulesParser` resolves the `Location` header and re-fetches the target for up to fiv
items.summary: Description When StormCrawler fetches a host's `/robots.txt` and receives a redirect, `HttpRobotRulesParser` resolves the `Location` header and re-fetches the target for up to five hops. The loop checks neither the scheme, the host nor the port of the resolved target, and it is not governed by `http.allow.redirects`, which only affects the page fetch. A crawled site can therefore point the robots.txt fetch at any address reachable from the fetcher worker, including loopback interfaces, private ranges and cloud metadata endpoints. Every crawled URL triggers a robots.txt fetch on a cache miss, so no unusual configuration is required to reach the loop. The fetched body is only parsed as robots rules and is not returned to the caller, so the read itself is blind. The more direct impact is on credentials: the okhttp protocol applies its configured request headers, including the `Authorization` header built from `http.basicauth.user` and `http.basicauth.password` and anything in `http.custom.headers`, to every request it makes. items.title: CVE-2026-59415: TypesenseVectorStore is vulnerable to a document ID injection in its delete operation that can cause unintended documents to be deleted. TypesenseVectorStore.doDelete(List<Stri
items.summary: TypesenseVectorStore is vulnerable to a document ID injection in its delete operation that can cause unintended documents to be deleted. TypesenseVectorStore.doDelete(List ) builds a Typesense filter_by expression by raw string concatenation of caller-supplied document IDs into the form id: [id1,id2,...] . The Typesense id field uses bare (unquoted) values in this list form with no escaping mechanism. An ID containing characters with syntactic meaning in the Typesense filter grammar — such as a comma ( , ), a closing bracket ( ] ), or operator tokens ( || , && ) — can break out of the list literal and alter the structure of the filter expression. An attacker who controls a document ID passed to the delete operation can use this to delete documents other than the intended ones (comma injection), or to construct a filter that matches every document in the collection (operator breakout), resulting in unintended bulk deletion. Applications that pass externally supplied or user-controlled document IDs to VectorStore.delete(List ) backed by TypesenseVectorStore are affected.

The mirror-image configuration, naming only `ignoreOutsideHost`, fails with a `NullPointerException` while the topology is starting. Projects generated from the StormCrawler Maven archetypes are not affected, because all three shipped filter configurations set both parameters. items.title: CVE-2026-112788: Missing Authentication for Critical Function in Apache Texera (incubating). The Python virtual environment (PVE) management endpoints of a computing unit are not authenticated b
items.summary: Missing Authentication for Critical Function in Apache Texera (incubating). The Python virtual environment (PVE) management endpoints of a computing unit are not authenticated by the application itself. In the local JVM and single-node Docker Compose deployments, which place no authenticating gateway in front of the services, these endpoints are reachable without credentials. The Kubernetes deployment gates them at the gateway, so only the Kubernetes deployment provides the full security model described in SECURITY.md. This issue affects Apache Texera (incubating): from 1.1.0 through 1.2.0. Users are recommended to use the Kubernetes deployment, which enforces the full security model, and to upgrade to 1.3.0-incubating, which documents that the local JVM and single-node Docker Compose deployments do not provide the full security model and should only be used by trusted users.

No authentication is required when the authorization feature is not enabled. items.summary: A reflected cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability exists in the initialization component of ADM. Affected products and versions include: from ADM 4.1.0 through ADM 4.3.3.RY62 as well as from ADM 5.0.0 through ADM 5.1.4.RM62.

items.title: CVE-2026-135801: Since the fix for CVE-2025-64500, Request::getPathInfo() strips the script name from the start of the URL. It does so even when the script name is only the start of a longer path s
items.summary: Since the fix for CVE-2025-64500, Request::getPathInfo() strips the script name from the start of the URL. It does so even when the script name is only the start of a longer path segment. With SCRIPT_NAME set to /index.php, a request to /index.phpadmin gets the path info /admin and is routed like /admin. Encoded spellings such as /index%2Ephpadmin or /%69ndex.phpadmin work too. Before that fix, the path info was admin, which no route matched. Rules enforced by Symfony are not affected: access_control and firewalls read the same path info as the router. Rules enforced in front of PHP are. The nginx configuration of the Symfony documentation and the .htaccess file of symfony/apache-pack make /index.php/admin unreachable, but they pass /index.phpadmin to the front controller. So a location /admin block in nginx, a section in Apache, or a CDN or WAF rule on /admin can be bypassed. The script name is now stripped only when it is followed by /, ? or the end of the URL. A request to /index.phpadmin gets the path info /index.phpadmin.

items.title: CVE-2026-135802: When Request::getBaseUrl() does not find the script name at the start of the request URI, it looks for it further into the path. This supports web servers that rewrite every URL to
items.summary: When Request::getBaseUrl() does not find the script name at the start of the request URI, it looks for it further into the path. This supports web servers that rewrite every URL to a front controller in a subdirectory. The base URL then kept everything before the script name, and the client chooses that part. A request URI starting with // or /\ made the base URL start with a host. With SCRIPT_NAME=/public/index.php, a request for //evil.example/public/index.php/login is routed to /login, with the base URL //evil.example/public/index.php and the base path //evil.example/public. The attacker has to make a user follow a crafted link, such as https://app.example//evil.example/public/index.php/login. framework.trusted_hosts does not help, since the host of the request is the real one. items.title: CVE-2026-135803: Most methods of Symfony\Component\Filesystem\Path rely on Path::split(), which takes everything before the first :// as the root of a path. It doesn't check that this prefix is a U
items.summary: Most methods of Symfony\Component\Filesystem\Path rely on Path::split(), which takes everything before the first :// as the root of a path. It doesn't check that this prefix is a URI scheme, so the .. segments in that prefix are never resolved. PHP sees a scheme only at the start of a string. So /base/../x://../secret.txt is a plain local path to /secret.txt for PHP, while Path::isBasePath('/base', '/base/../x://../secret.txt') returns true. canonicalize(), join(), makeAbsolute() and makeRelative() are affected the same way. Some applications check a path built from user input with isBasePath() or canonicalize(), and then open it. They can be made to read or write files outside the expected directory. On Symfony 6.4 and later, the AssetMapper component builds with Path::join() the path of the files that a remote package references from its CSS. A malicious or compromised package can therefore make importmap:require or importmap:install write a file of its choice outside assets/vendor. For example, the CSS url(../../../../../public/x://shell.php) writes public/x:/shell.php. A prefix is now a scheme only when PHP would look for a stream wrapper with that name. items.title: CVE-2026-135804: The fix for CVE-2026-45756 lowers pcre.backtrack_limit to 10000 around each preg_match() call of the match() and search() filter functions. That limit applies to one starting posit
items.summary: The fix for CVE-2026-45756 lowers pcre.backtrack_limit to 10000 around each preg_match() call of the match() and search() filter functions. That limit applies to one starting position, not to one call. PCRE resets its counter at every position it tries a match from. So an unanchored pattern that stays just under the limit is paid once per byte of the subject. Each call also starts from a fresh limit, so chaining clauses in one filter multiplies the work. Two other paths made the cost of a query grow faster than its size, without any regular expression: - The filter evaluator scanned the whole expression for logical operators once per node. Its cost grew with the square of the number of chained clauses. - Queries starting with $ inside a filter, like @.x == $.limit or length($.items), were evaluated again for every node the filter visits. An application that evaluates an attacker-influenced JSONPath expression can therefore still be made to hold a PHP worker. A document of 2 MB and a query of 2.5 KB take 3.5 minutes of CPU. items.title: CVE-2026-133775: The fix for CVE-2026-55877 (GHSA-6v8j-33hc-mv84) sanitizes the SVG of icons before they are rendered inline. It removes scripts and event handlers everywhere, except inside
items.summary: The fix for CVE-2026-55877 (GHSA-6v8j-33hc-mv84) sanitizes the SVG of icons before they are rendered inline. It removes scripts and event handlers everywhere, except inside elements. Unlike in HTML, the content of an SVG element is parsed as markup. An icon can therefore still run JavaScript in the page with, for example: alert(1) Applications are exposed when an attacker can influence the SVG of the icons they render. The sources are the same as for CVE-2026-55877, like local icon files and the responses of the Iconify API. elements are now sanitized like any other element, so their descendants lose scripts and event handlers. A element that tries to close itself early is still removed. Otherwise, its CSS is kept.

items.title: CVE-2026-133776: The fix for CVE-2026-55877 (GHSA-6v8j-33hc-mv84) sanitizes the SVG of icons before they are rendered inline. When the sanitizer changes an icon, it writes the icon out again as HTM
items.summary: The fix for CVE-2026-55877 (GHSA-6v8j-33hc-mv84) sanitizes the SVG of icons before they are rendered inline. When the sanitizer changes an icon, it writes the icon out again as HTML. HTML writes the content of some elements, like , without escaping it. But inside an , browsers parse the content of a element as markup. Escaped markup in such an element then becomes live in the page: The event handler of the element only makes the sanitizer change the icon. Depending on the version, this affects every element, or the elements of the XHTML namespace, like , or . On 2.x, the elements of the XHTML namespace were also kept. An XHTML or element then becomes live where icons are parsed as XML, like in the Google Maps bridge of ux-map. Applications are exposed when an attacker can influence the SVG of the icons they render. The sources are the same as for CVE-2026-55877, like local icon files and the responses of the Iconify API. On 2.x, the sanitizer now writes icons out as XML, which escapes their text, and only keeps the elements of the SVG namespace. On 3.x, it now only keeps the elements of the SVG namespace.

items.summary: The fix for CVE-2026-55877 (GHSA-6v8j-33hc-mv84) sanitizes the SVG of icons before they are rendered inline. It could also add a element that redirects the page. Comments were kept too, while browsers end a comment at or . The rest of such a comment then became live markup, even without any HTML element before it. Applications are exposed when an attacker can influence the SVG of the icons they render. The sources are the same as for CVE-2026-55877, like local icon files and the responses of the Iconify API. items.title: CVE-2026-133778: #[AsLiveComponent(route: '...')] makes a live component send its requests to another route. The documentation suggests it so that the component lives under a specific firewall, for
items.summary: #[AsLiveComponent(route: '...')] makes a live component send its requests to another route. The documentation suggests it so that the component lives under a specific firewall, for example. The default /_components/{_live_component}/{_live_action} route still served the component, though. A request to it rendered the component and ran its actions outside the firewall and the access rules of the configured route. The request needs props signed by the application, which a page that rendered the component provides. Controller attributes on the component, like #[IsGranted], still applied. A live component is now only served by the route it is configured with.

items.title: CVE-2026-133779: The fix for CVE-2026-55877 (GHSA-6v8j-33hc-mv84) sanitizes the SVG of icons before they are rendered inline. The checks matched attribute names as written in the icon, while browse
items.summary: The fix for CVE-2026-55877 (GHSA-6v8j-33hc-mv84) sanitizes the SVG of icons before they are rendered inline. The checks matched attribute names as written in the icon, while browsers and the renderer read some names differently. On 2.x, fromFile() keys the attributes of the root element by their local name. A handler like x:onload passed the check, and was then rendered as onload, which runs on load. HTML parsers also read attribute names case-insensitively, so a SMIL animation with ATTRIBUTENAME="href" could set a javascript: URL on a link. And an href in the XLink namespace under another prefix, like q:href, wasn't checked. On 3.x, the sanitizer writes it out as xlink:href, and XML parsers resolve the prefix on both branches. Applications are exposed when an attacker can influence the SVG of the icons they render. The sources are the same as for CVE-2026-55877, like local icon files and the responses of the Iconify API. The sanitizer now checks attributes by local name. It also finds the attributeName of animations in any case, and ignores the prefix of its value.

items.title: CVE-2026-133780: The @symfony/stimulus-bridge npm package includes a Webpack loader called lazy-controller-loader that supports "magic comments" placed above a Stimulus controller import, for examp
items.summary: The @symfony/stimulus-bridge npm package includes a Webpack loader called lazy-controller-loader that supports "magic comments" placed above a Stimulus controller import, for example /* stimulusFetch: 'lazy' */, to control lazy loading behavior. To read those options, the loader extracted the raw text of any stimulus* comment and evaluated it as JavaScript using Node's vm.runInNewContext(). The Node.js node:vm module is not a security sandbox, and a crafted comment can break out of the VM context using well-known techniques to run arbitrary Node.js code within the build process. This is a build-time vulnerability: it does not affect browsers or end users. The code executes on the developer machine or CI/build server during a Webpack or Symfony Encore build. Realistic attack vectors include a malicious Stimulus controller introduced through a compromised dependency, or a pull request that triggers an automated CI build. An attacker who can get such a file into the build can read files and environment variables available to the build process, exfiltrate CI secrets, tamper with generated build artifacts, and run commands with the permissions of the build user. The loader no longer eva

items.title: CVE-2026-133781: The controllers.json loader of @symfony/stimulus-bridge loads the package.json file of each package listed in controllers.json with require(). Node resolves this path through the e
items.summary: The controllers.json loader of @symfony/stimulus-bridge loads the package.json file of each package listed in controllers.json with require(). Node resolves this path through the exports field of the package, which can map ./package.json to a script. require() then runs that script during the Webpack or Symfony Encore build. This is a build-time vulnerability: it doesn't affect browsers or end users. A malicious or compromised package listed in controllers.json can run code on the developer machine or the CI server. This works even when the package manager doesn't run install scripts. This code can read the files and environment variables of the build, like CI secrets, and change the built assets. The loader now reads the resolved file and parses it as JSON, so that a mapped script fails to parse instead of running.

items.title: CVE-2026-133774: A live component protected by #[IsGranted], on its class or on its default action, can be rendered by a caller who is not granted access. POST /_components/{name}/_batch is handled
items.summary: A live component protected by #[IsGranted], on its class or on its default action, can be rendered by a caller who is not granted access. POST /_components/{name}/_batch is handled by Symfony\UX\LiveComponent\Controller\BatchActionController, which has no controller attributes: the attributes of the component are only checked by the sub-request issued for each action. With an empty actions list, no sub-request was issued, and the hydrated component was rendered and returned with a 200. The caller needs a valid signed props payload for the component, such as the data-live-props-value of a page that rendered it: one the caller could see before losing access, or a cached or shared page. The checksum binds the props to the component name, not to a user, a session or a time, so such a payload can be replayed. Actions are not affected, since each action of a non-empty batch is still checked in its own sub-request. Components that load data from their props, like an entity identifier, disclose that data to the caller. BatchActionController now rejects a batch without any action with a BadRequestHttpException. items.summary: A cleartext transmission of sensitive information vulnerability in the ADM Notifications allows network eavesdroppers on the outbound network path to obtain Clickatell service credentials via the SMS. When executing an SMS test for Clickatell Communicator Central, the backend function Send_Test_SMS embeds the sensitive contents directly into an unencrypted HTTP request URL. An observer on the NAS network egress path can capture the plain text credentials and message payload since the initial request is transmitted without TLS protection or secret redaction. Affected products and versions include: from ADM 4.1.0 through ADM 4.3.3.RY62 as well as from ADM 5.0.0 through ADM 5.1.4.RM62.

items.title: CVE-2026-134897: An OS command injection vulnerability in ADM allows an authenticated administrator to create an iSCSI LUN with a crafted name and schedule a snapshot. The scheduler embeds the name
items.summary: An OS command injection vulnerability in ADM allows an authenticated administrator to create an iSCSI LUN with a crafted name and schedule a snapshot. The scheduler embeds the name in a root cron job without correctly neutralizing shell metacharacters, allowing arbitrary command execution as root when the job runs. items.title: CVE-2026-135779: Reliance on an untrusted source of the client address in the WebSocket listener of the NetBird relay server (relay/server/listener/ws) in NetBird versions 0.31.1 through 0.74.7 all
items.summary: Reliance on an untrusted source of the client address in the WebSocket listener of the NetBird relay server (relay/server/listener/ws) in NetBird versions 0.31.1 through 0.74.7 allows an attacker with an enrolled peer to spoof the source address of their relay connection. The listener used the values of the X-Real-Ip and X-Real-Port request headers as the remote address of the connection unconditionally, without checking that the request came from a trusted upstream proxy. A WebSocket client that sends both headers makes the relay record and use an arbitrary address for its connection, including in the relay connection log, so a client can hide its real address or attribute its connection to another host. Only the relay server is affected; the NetBird client, including the Android and iOS apps, does not run the relay listener. The issue is fixed in version 0.75.0, which honours these headers only for requests whose direct connection address is in a configured set of trusted proxies and ignores them by default.

Affected products and versions include: from ADM 4.1.0 through ADM 4.3.3.RY62 as well as from ADM 5.0.0 through ADM 5.1.4.RM62.

items.title: CVE-2026-105431: A protection mechanism failure in the userspace firewall of the NetBird client (client/firewall/uspfilter) in NetBird versions 0.55.0 through 0.74.6 allows an attacker who controls
items.summary: A protection mechanism failure in the userspace firewall of the NetBird client (client/firewall/uspfilter) in NetBird versions 0.55.0 through 0.74.6 allows an attacker who controls an enrolled peer to bypass the access control rules of another peer by sending IP-fragmented packets. The packet filter returned an allow verdict for any IPv4 fragment, and for any IPv6 packet carrying a Fragment extension header, before evaluating the ACL rules. This applied to the leading fragment as well as to continuation fragments, so no part of a fragmented datagram was filtered and ports denied by policy could be reached. The userspace filter is the packet filter wherever the client does not program the kernel firewall, which includes the Android and iOS apps. The issue is fixed in version 0.74.7, in the Android app from version 0.6.0 and in the iOS app from version 0.3.3, which evaluate fragments against the same ACL rules as unfragmented packets.

items.title: CVE-2026-120934: An External Control of File Name or Path (Argument Injection) vulnerability in the settings/notification.cgi component of ADM allows authenticated remote administrators to create o
items.summary: An External Control of File Name or Path (Argument Injection) vulnerability in the settings/notification.cgi component of ADM allows authenticated remote administrators to create or truncate arbitrary files with root privileges via crafted request parameters. An authenticated administrator can truncate arbitrary critical files across the root filesystem, leading to system failure or Denial of Service (DoS). items.title: CVE-2026-120935: An argument injection vulnerability exists in the settings/vpn.cgi endpoint in the ADM. When processing a WireGuard profile, the internal command parser removes quotes and performs
items.summary: An argument injection vulnerability exists in the settings/vpn.cgi endpoint in the ADM. When processing a WireGuard profile, the internal command parser removes quotes and performs a quote-agnostic scan on arguments without properly sanitizing redirection operators. An authenticated administrator can supply a crafted parameter to cause the execution helper to open and truncate arbitrary files on the filesystem with root privileges, resulting in an arbitrary file truncation and denial-of-service (DoS) condition. Affected products and versions include: from ADM 4.1.0 through ADM 4.3.3.RY62 as well as from ADM 5.0.0 through ADM 5.1.4.RM62.

items.title: CVE-2026-120936: An arbitrary file creation and truncation vulnerability exists in the File Explorer of ADM. An authenticated low-privileged user can upload a file with crafted path components cont
items.summary: An arbitrary file creation and truncation vulnerability exists in the File Explorer of ADM. An authenticated low-privileged user can upload a file with crafted path components containing quote and redirection characters. When music.cgi processes the entry for audio playback operations, the unescaped path string breaks out of the expected argument context in the internal command parser. This causes the system execution helper to open the attacker-specified path with root privileges using O_TRUNC, allowing remote attackers to truncate or create arbitrary system files. Affected products and versions include: from ADM 4.1.0 through ADM 4.3.3.RY62 as well as from ADM 5.0.0 through ADM 5.1.4.RM62.
