items.title: CVE-2026-135259: MISP contains a type confusion vulnerability in the authentication key creation endpoint. When a user submits a floating-point value as the target user identifier, the authorizatio
items.summary: MISP contains a type confusion vulnerability in the authentication key creation endpoint. When a user submits a floating-point value as the target user identifier, the authorization check truncates the value to an integer (matching the attacker's own account), while the persistence layer rounds the same value to a different integer (the next account in the sequence). This discrepancy allows an authenticated user with key-creation permission to generate an API authentication key belonging to another user. Preconditions: - The attacker must be an authenticated user with the permission to create authentication keys. - The target user must have a consecutive numeric identifier immediately following the attacker's identifier. Impact: - Unauthorized creation of an API key for another user, granting the attacker access to that user's data and operations within the MISP instance. - The vulnerability is trivially exploitable by substituting a carefully crafted floating-point value for the integer user identifier in the request. Affected versions: MISP prior to 2.5.52.

items.title: CVE-2026-135249: MISP accepted compressed HTTP request bodies (gzip, brotli, zstd) and decompressed them before authentication was performed, with no limit on the size of the resulting decompressed
items.summary: MISP accepted compressed HTTP request bodies (gzip, brotli, zstd) and decompressed them before authentication was performed, with no limit on the size of the resulting decompressed data. An unauthenticated attacker could send a small compressed payload that expands to a very large decompressed body, exhausting server memory and causing a denial of service. Brotli and zstd, with their high compression ratios, made the attack particularly effective. The vulnerability required no authentication and no special conditions beyond the ability to send an HTTP request with a Content-Encoding header. The impact is a complete loss of availability for the affected MISP instance. Affected: MISP versions prior to 2.5.52.

items.title: CVE-2026-135250: MISP contains a denial-of-service vulnerability in its image processing pipeline. When generating attachment thumbnails or rendering event graph preview images, the application dec
items.summary: MISP contains a denial-of-service vulnerability in its image processing pipeline. When generating attachment thumbnails or rendering event graph preview images, the application decodes user-supplied image data using the GD library without first validating the declared pixel dimensions in the image header. Because GD allocates its pixel buffers outside the scope of PHP's memory_limit directive, a crafted image with an extremely large declared resolution (for example, 20000 x 20000 pixels) can trigger a multi-gigabyte memory allocation during the decode step, exhausting available system memory and causing the PHP worker process or the host to become unresponsive. Preconditions: - An authenticated MISP user with permission to upload attachments or to create/view event graphs. - The ability to supply a crafted image file (e.g., a PNG with a valid header declaring oversized dimensions). Impact: - Denial of service: memory exhaustion leading to process crash or host unavailability. - No confidentiality or integrity impact is indicated by the evidence. Affected versions: MISP prior to 2.5.52.

items.title: CVE-2026-135252: MISP contains a Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) vulnerability in its feed and sync HTTP request handling. When the application uses libcurl as the HTTP transport, the CURLOPT_FO
items.summary: MISP contains a Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) vulnerability in its feed and sync HTTP request handling. When the application uses libcurl as the HTTP transport, the CURLOPT_FOLLOWLOCATION option was enabled by default, causing the library to automatically follow HTTP redirects without the application's own per-hop validation logic being invoked. - Feed requests: MISP implements its own redirect validation for feed sources, but libcurl was following redirects before that validation could execute, allowing a malicious or compromised feed source to redirect the request to arbitrary internal URLs. - Sync requests: Sync peers are server-configured, and the application does not perform per-hop redirect validation for sync traffic. libcurl's automatic redirect following allowed a malicious sync peer to redirect the request to internal network resources. An attacker who is a configured sync peer, controls a feed source URL, or can influence DNS resolution for a configured endpoint can exploit this to cause the MISP server to issue requests to arbitrary internal services, potentially reading sensitive data or interacting with internal APIs that are not otherwise exposed. Affected: MISP

items.title: CVE-2026-135253: MISP's NIDS rule export functionality for Snort and Suricata formats does not properly escape user-controlled data before embedding it into generated rule text. Attribute values, t
items.summary: MISP's NIDS rule export functionality for Snort and Suricata formats does not properly escape user-controlled data before embedding it into generated rule text. Attribute values, tag names, and URL paths are inserted directly into rule options (msg, metadata, content matches) without neutralizing characters that are syntactically significant in the NIDS rule grammar, such as double quotes, semicolons, backslashes, commas, and control characters. An authenticated user with the ability to create or modify attributes in a MISP instance can craft attribute values or tag names containing these special characters. When the NIDS rules are exported, the unescaped data breaks out of the intended option or content field, allowing injection of arbitrary rule options, corruption of rule structure, or generation of syntactically invalid rules that may cause the downstream NIDS engine to reject the entire ruleset. The affected export paths include: - Snort and Suricata msg: option (quotes, semicolons, backslashes, control characters) - Suricata metadata: option (commas, semicolons, quotes, whitespace, control characters) - Suricata http.uri content: match for URL path (quotes, semicolons, pipe c

items.title: CVE-2026-135254: MISP is vulnerable to Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) in its correlation management functionality. The top-correlation cache regeneration and occurrence count regeneration actio
items.summary: MISP is vulnerable to Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) in its correlation management functionality. The top-correlation cache regeneration and occurrence count regeneration actions were accessible via bodyless GET requests and were triggered from the admin interface using plain hyperlinks rather than POST forms. Because these state-changing operations did not require a POST method and were reachable through simple URL navigation, an attacker who can induce an authenticated administrator to visit a malicious page or click a crafted link can trigger these operations without the administrator's explicit consent. Impact: - Unintended triggering of resource-intensive correlation regeneration processes - Potential disruption of correlation data processing and increased server load - No direct data disclosure or corruption is evidenced Affected: MISP versions prior to 2.5.52

items.title: CVE-2026-135243: MISP contains an authorization bypass vulnerability in the handling of sightings during server synchronization and bulk operations. The vulnerability allows a remote attacker with
items.summary: MISP contains an authorization bypass vulnerability in the handling of sightings during server synchronization and bulk operations. The vulnerability allows a remote attacker with access to a synchronized MISP instance to pull sightings for events that are not shared with their organization or community. The sighting pull mechanism previously executed with elevated privileges and accepted event identifiers without verifying that the local event was authorized for sharing with the remote server. Additionally, the bulk save functionality for sightings did not strictly enforce that the attributes referenced in the request belonged to the specific event specified in the URL, allowing an attacker to associate sightings with unauthorized events by referencing attributes from other events. This can lead to unauthorized disclosure of threat intelligence data and integrity issues where sightings are incorrectly attributed to events the attacker should not access. The issue was reported by ENISA and fixed in version 2.5.52.

items.title: CVE-2026-135244: MISP trusted client-supplied forwarded IP headers (such as X-Forwarded-For) without verifying that the request originated from a known proxy or that the value was a valid IP addres
items.summary: MISP trusted client-supplied forwarded IP headers (such as X-Forwarded-For) without verifying that the request originated from a known proxy or that the value was a valid IP address. The configured header value was accepted as the authoritative client IP for all security-relevant functions. An unauthenticated remote attacker could forge the forwarded header to: - Bypass IP-based restrictions on API authentication keys - Evade brute-force / rate-limiting protection - Inject arbitrary values into application and ECS logs, corrupting audit trails The vulnerability required the MISP.log_client_ip_header setting to be configured to a forwarded header (e.g. HTTP_X_FORWARDED_FOR), which is a common deployment when MISP sits behind a reverse proxy. Affected: MISP versions prior to 2.5.52

items.title: CVE-2026-135245: MISP's LDAP authentication components (LdapAuth plugin and Apache LDAP authentication) unconditionally re-enabled user accounts that had been disabled by an administrator. During t
items.summary: MISP's LDAP authentication components (LdapAuth plugin and Apache LDAP authentication) unconditionally re-enabled user accounts that had been disabled by an administrator. During the user provisioning or update step of an LDAP login, the disabled flag was reset to enabled regardless of the account's current state. This allowed any user with valid LDAP credentials to bypass an administrative disable action simply by authenticating, effectively nullifying the ability to revoke access through account deactivation. - Affects the LdapAuth plugin and the ApacheSecureAuth component - The insecure behavior was the default; no special configuration was required to trigger it - An administrator's decision to disable a user (e.g., after a security incident or employee departure) could be reversed by the user's next successful LDAP login Affected versions: MISP prior to 2.5.52

items.title: CVE-2026-135247: MISP's LinOTPAuth plugin, used for one-time-password authentication against a LinOTP server, did not enforce TLS server certificate verification when the LinOTPAuth.verifyssl confi
items.summary: MISP's LinOTPAuth plugin, used for one-time-password authentication against a LinOTP server, did not enforce TLS server certificate verification when the LinOTPAuth.verifyssl configuration option was not explicitly set. In a default or minimally configured deployment, the authentication request to the LinOTP server was sent without peer or peer-name certificate validation, effectively allowing self-signed or spoofed certificates. An attacker with a network position between the MISP instance and the LinOTP server could perform a man-in-the-middle attack to intercept or tamper with the authentication exchange, potentially capturing one-time passwords or user credentials. Preconditions: - The LinOTPAuth plugin is enabled and configured to communicate with a LinOTP server - The LinOTPAuth.verifyssl setting is absent or null (not explicitly set to true or false) - The attacker can position themselves on the network path between MISP and the LinOTP server Security impact: - Confidentiality of OTP tokens and authentication credentials in transit - Potential for credential interception or replay Affected versions: MISP prior to 2.5.52

items.title: CVE-2026-135248: MISP contains a vulnerability in its password reset (forgot password) functionality where the base URL used to construct the reset link sent by email could be derived from the HTTP
items.summary: MISP contains a vulnerability in its password reset (forgot password) functionality where the base URL used to construct the reset link sent by email could be derived from the HTTP request's Host header rather than from an explicitly configured value. An unauthenticated attacker can send a crafted request with a malicious Host header. If the application's base URL was not explicitly configured (MISP.baseurl or MISP.external_baseurl), the bootstrap would derive it from the request, and the resulting password reset email would contain a link pointing to the attacker-controlled domain. When the victim clicks the link, they are directed to the attacker's site, enabling credential phishing or token theft. Preconditions: - The password reset feature (allow_password_forgotten) is enabled - MISP.baseurl and MISP.external_baseurl are not explicitly set to trusted values - The victim initiates or is targeted for a password reset Impact: - Phishing: victim is redirected to an attacker-controlled URL instead of the legitimate MISP instance - Potential credential compromise if the victim enters credentials on the attacker's site - No direct compromise of the MISP server itself Affected: MISP ve

items.title: CVE-2026-135239: MISP contains an authorization flaw in the data capture and import paths for events, galaxies, galaxy clusters, analyst data, and sightings. A user who is neither a sync user nor a
items.summary: MISP contains an authorization flaw in the data capture and import paths for events, galaxies, galaxy clusters, analyst data, and sightings. A user who is neither a sync user nor a site admin could create or import records attributed to an organisation other than their own, or cause the creation of a new organisation from a payload-supplied identifier. The root cause is an inconsistent authorization check: the code validated one representation of the creator organisation (for example a numeric ID or a UUID field) while storing a different representation taken directly from the user-supplied payload. In the event import path, a MISP export naming another organisation or a fabricated one was accepted and stored under that organisation. In the galaxy, cluster, analyst data, and sighting capture paths, the nested organisation object from the payload was used to create or reference an organisation without verifying the caller's membership. Impact: - Data (events, galaxies, clusters, analyst notes, sightings) can be created under an organisation the attacker does not belong to, polluting that organisation's data and potentially exposing it to that organisation's members. - New organisati

items.title: CVE-2026-135240: MISP contains an authorization bypass in its tag attachment functionality. The endpoints responsible for editing event tags, editing attribute tags, and adding tags to event report
items.summary: MISP contains an authorization bypass in its tag attachment functionality. The endpoints responsible for editing event tags, editing attribute tags, and adding tags to event reports accepted arbitrary tag IDs without verifying whether the authenticated user was permitted to attach the referenced tag. The events/addTag endpoint already resolved tag IDs through a restricted lookup that enforced per-user and per-organisation tag visibility rules. However, the three tag-editor endpoints (editEventTags, editAttributeTags, and eventReports/addTag) passed the supplied tag IDs directly to the attachment logic without any such check. Preconditions: - An authenticated user with tagger and add permissions on the target event/attribute/report. - Knowledge or discovery of a tag ID that is restricted (local_only) to another organisation. Impact: - A user can attach a tag that is restricted to a different organisation, effectively bypassing the tag visibility and scoping model. - A local_only tag can be attached as a global tag, violating the intended distribution restriction and potentially exposing the existence or semantics of another organisation's restricted tag to a broader audience. - Data

items.title: CVE-2026-135241: MISP contains an authorization bypass vulnerability in the handling of Galaxy and Galaxy Cluster publish/unpublish operations. The application failed to enforce consistent permissi
items.summary: MISP contains an authorization bypass vulnerability in the handling of Galaxy and Galaxy Cluster publish/unpublish operations. The application failed to enforce consistent permission checks when users attempted to unpublish a Galaxy or Galaxy Cluster. Specifically, the unpublish action only required the 'perm_galaxy_editor' permission, whereas the publish action required both 'perm_galaxy_editor' and 'perm_publish'. This inconsistency allowed a user from a different organization who possessed the 'perm_galaxy_editor' permission but lacked the 'perm_publish' permission to unpublish a Galaxy or Galaxy Cluster created by another organization. This action could disrupt the availability of shared threat intelligence data for other users and organizations relying on that cluster. The vulnerability affects MISP versions prior to 2.5.52.

items.title: CVE-2026-135242: MISP contains an authorization flaw in the Sharing Group Blueprint execution path. When a blueprint is executed, it rewrites the organisation roster of the associated sharing group
items.summary: MISP contains an authorization flaw in the Sharing Group Blueprint execution path. When a blueprint is executed, it rewrites the organisation roster of the associated sharing group. The check verifying that the blueprint's owning organisation still holds the right to extend (modify) that group was performed only once, at the time the blueprint was created. It was not re-evaluated at execution time. As a result, an organisation that subsequently lost its extend permission or was entirely removed from the sharing group could still execute its existing blueprint and overwrite the group's organisation roster, adding or removing member organisations at will. Preconditions: - An authenticated user belonging to an organisation that previously had extend rights on a sharing group - A blueprint already exists in that group owned by the attacker's organisation - The attacker's extend rights have been revoked or the organisation has been removed from the group after the blueprint was created Security impact: - Unauthorised modification of a sharing group's organisation roster - Potential unauthorised addition of organisations to a sharing group, exposing shared indicators and events - Bypass

items.title: CVE-2026-135237: MISP contains a DOM-based Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) vulnerability in the event report element rendering pipeline. The client-side sanitization function used to prepare values for
items.summary: MISP contains a DOM-based Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) vulnerability in the event report element rendering pipeline. The client-side sanitization function used to prepare values for doT templates only escaped ampersand, less-than, and greater-than characters. However, the templates place these values inside double-quoted HTML attributes. Because double-quote and single-quote characters were not escaped, a user with the ability to author or modify report element values could inject a quote character to break out of the attribute context and inject arbitrary HTML or JavaScript that executes in the viewing user's browser. Preconditions: - The attacker must be an authenticated user with permission to create or edit event report elements (e.g., a report author). - A victim must open or view the crafted report in a browser. Security impact: - Execution of arbitrary JavaScript in the context of the victim's MISP session. - Potential theft of session tokens, sensitive data, or unauthorized actions performed on behalf of the victim. Affected versions: MISP prior to 2.5.52.

items.title: CVE-2026-135238: MISP contains a cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability in the Overmind server preview's analyst data badge component. When rendering the analyst data link for a remote attribute,
items.summary: MISP contains a cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability in the Overmind server preview's analyst data badge component. When rendering the analyst data link for a remote attribute, the remote server's UUID value was inserted into an inline JavaScript event handler using only HTML entity encoding, which is insufficient to prevent breakout from the JavaScript string context within the HTML attribute. An attacker who can control or influence the UUID value of a remote attribute (for example, through a malicious or compromised upstream MISP server sharing data via Overmind) could inject arbitrary JavaScript that executes in the context of the victim's MISP session when the analyst data badge is clicked. Preconditions: - The victim must be authenticated to a MISP instance with Overmind enabled. - The victim must view a remote event preview containing the crafted UUID. - The victim must interact with (click) the analyst data badge element. Security impact: - Execution of arbitrary JavaScript in the victim's browser session. - Potential theft of session credentials, manipulation of page content, or initiation of unauthorized actions on behalf of the authenticated user. Affected versions:

items.title: CVE-2026-135234: MISP contains a cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability in the feed and server event preview pages. When a remote MISP instance (configured as a feed source or connected server) s
items.summary: MISP contains a cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability in the feed and server event preview pages. When a remote MISP instance (configured as a feed source or connected server) supplies object or reference UUIDs and IDs containing special characters, these values are rendered in the preview HTML without proper escaping. The vulnerable behavior occurs in two contexts: - HTML element identifiers and text content: Remote UUIDs and IDs are inserted into DOM element IDs and visible text without HTML encoding, allowing injection of arbitrary HTML markup. - Inline JavaScript event handlers: Remote UUIDs and IDs are embedded into onClick handler strings using only HTML escaping, which does not protect against JavaScript string-literal breakout. A crafted value containing a single quote can terminate the string and inject arbitrary JavaScript. An attacker who controls a remote MISP instance (feed or server peer) can craft UUID or ID fields with a malicious payload. When an authenticated user on the victim instance views the corresponding event preview, the injected script executes in the user's browser within the MISP application origin, potentially allowing session hijacking, data exfilt

items.title: CVE-2026-135235: MISP contains a stored cross-site script (XSS) vulnerability in the event review page used for merge, import, and enrichment workflows. Object references displayed on this page in
items.summary: MISP contains a stored cross-site script (XSS) vulnerability in the event review page used for merge, import, and enrichment workflows. Object references displayed on this page include the UUID, name, and meta-category of the referenced object. These values originate from imported data (another event, a module result, or an import file) and were rendered into the HTML output without any encoding or sanitization. An attacker who can supply or influence imported MISP-format data can embed arbitrary HTML or JavaScript in the referenced object's UUID, name, or meta-category fields. When a user views the review page, the malicious script executes in the user's browser context. Preconditions: - The attacker must be able to introduce data into a MISP instance (e.g., via import, module enrichment, or event merge). - A victim user must open the affected review page in a browser. Security impact: - Execution of arbitrary JavaScript in the context of the MISP web application. - Potential theft of session tokens, manipulation of user actions, or exfiltration of sensitive threat-intelligence data visible on the page. Affected versions: MISP prior to 2.5.52.

items.title: CVE-2026-135236: MISP contains a stored cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability in its map attachment rendering. When a GPX or GeoJSON file is uploaded as an attachment to a MISP event, the waypoi
items.summary: MISP contains a stored cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability in its map attachment rendering. When a GPX or GeoJSON file is uploaded as an attachment to a MISP event, the waypoint names (GPX) and property names and values (GeoJSON) are inserted into Leaflet map popups without HTML escaping. Because Leaflet renders popup content as raw HTML, any markup or script embedded in those fields is executed in the browser of every user who views the map and interacts with the affected marker or icon. Preconditions: - An authenticated user with permission to upload attachments to a MISP event crafts a GPX or GeoJSON file containing malicious HTML/JavaScript in waypoint names or GeoJSON property keys/values. - A victim user views the event map and clicks the affected marker or GeoJSON icon, triggering the popup. Impact: - Execution of arbitrary JavaScript in the context of the MISP web application, potentially leading to session hijacking, data exfiltration, or unauthorized actions performed on behalf of the victim. Affected versions: MISP prior to 2.5.52.

items.title: CVE-2026-135213: Worklenz before 3.4.3 contains an insecure direct object reference vulnerability in GET /api/v1/activity-logs/:id that allows authenticated users to read other teams' task activity
items.summary: Worklenz before 3.4.3 contains an insecure direct object reference vulnerability in GET /api/v1/activity-logs/:id that allows authenticated users to read other teams' task activity logs because it lacks the verifyTaskAccess middleware. Attackers who know another team's task UUID can retrieve reporter and assignee names and avatars plus the full timeline of status, priority, label and estimation changes.

items.title: CVE-2026-135231: MISP contains an authorization bypass in the galaxy cluster detachment functionality. Users holding the sync role permission were incorrectly exempted from the tagger and organisat
items.summary: MISP contains an authorization bypass in the galaxy cluster detachment functionality. Users holding the sync role permission were incorrectly exempted from the tagger and organisation ownership checks when detaching galaxy clusters from events or attributes. This allowed a sync user belonging to one organisation to remove galaxy cluster associations (threat intelligence tags) from events and attributes owned by a different organisation. The sync permission was intended for replication workflows, which never invoke the cluster detachment code path, but was erroneously used as a blanket authorization bypass. Impact: - Cross-organisation data integrity: a sync user can strip threat intelligence cluster associations from other organisations' events and attributes. - Disruption of shared threat intelligence: removal of cluster tags can alter the analytical context of events visible to other users. Preconditions: - An authenticated user with the sync role permission (perm_sync) and tagger permission (perm_tagger). - The target event or attribute must belong to a different organisation than the attacker. Affected versions: MISP prior to 2.5.52.

items.title: CVE-2026-135232: MISP Collections retained a sharing group reference (sharing_group_id) even when the collection's distribution level was below 4 (i.e., not restricted to a sharing group). As a res
items.summary: MISP Collections retained a sharing group reference (sharing_group_id) even when the collection's distribution level was below 4 (i.e., not restricted to a sharing group). As a result, the sharing group name and UUID were displayed in the collection index and view endpoints to any user who could see the collection, regardless of whether that user was a member of the sharing group. Additionally, when collections were pushed to remote MISP servers, the sharing group data was included in the push payload even for collections not distributed to a sharing group, potentially leaking the group identity to remote systems. Preconditions: - An authenticated user with sufficient access to view the affected collection (e.g., a collection with distribution 0-3 that is publicly or broadly visible). - The collection must have a stale sharing_group_id stored from a prior save. Impact: - Unauthorized disclosure of the sharing group name and UUID to users outside the group. - Potential leakage of sharing group structure to remote MISP servers via the push mechanism. - An attacker could enumerate sharing group names to identify targeting opportunities. Affected versions: MISP prior to 2.5.52.

items.title: CVE-2026-135233: MISP's interactive CLI shell, when used to edit or disable a user account, did not update the user record's modification timestamp. The application's session validation mechanism r
items.summary: MISP's interactive CLI shell, when used to edit or disable a user account, did not update the user record's modification timestamp. The application's session validation mechanism relies on this timestamp to detect that a user's record has changed and to reload the user's state in all active sessions. As a result, a user who was disabled or had their role or permissions modified through the CLI would retain their existing authenticated session and continue to operate with their previous privileges until the session naturally expired. The administrative intent to revoke or reduce access was not enforced on already-active sessions. Preconditions: - An administrator performs a user edit or disable action via the MISP interactive CLI shell rather than the web interface. - The target user has one or more active web sessions at the time of the change. Impact: - A disabled user retains full access to the MISP instance for the duration of their existing session. - A user whose role or permissions were reduced via the CLI continues to operate with their prior, higher privileges in open sessions. Affected versions: MISP prior to 2.5.52.

items.title: CVE-2026-135207: Healthchecks before 4.4 contains a verification bypass vulnerability that allows project users to mark arbitrary email addresses as verified because Channel.make_token() omits the
items.summary: Healthchecks before 4.4 contains a verification bypass vulnerability that allows project users to mark arbitrary email addresses as verified because Channel.make_token() omits the email address. items.summary: ServerOS Panel before 1.10.1 contains a decompression bomb vulnerability in DeploySourcePacker::extract() that allows authenticated users with manage-machines permission to bypass the 4 GB unpacked-size limit by under-declaring zip entry sizes. items.summary: Plane before 1.5.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in WorkspaceDraftIssueViewSet that allows authenticated workspace members to create drafts in unauthorized projects by supplying an arbitrary project_id. Attackers can convert drafts into work items in private or removed-from projects with chosen title, state, assignees, cycle_id and module_ids, triggering notifications and disclosing project membership.

items.title: CVE-2026-135211: BISHENG before 3.0.0 contains a missing authentication vulnerability in the /api/v2/workflow/invoke and /api/v2/workflow/stop routes that allows unauthenticated attackers to run wo
items.summary: BISHENG before 3.0.0 contains a missing authentication vulnerability in the /api/v2/workflow/invoke and /api/v2/workflow/stop routes that allows unauthenticated attackers to run workflows as the administrator. items.summary: AiSOC before 23.6.1 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the agents service that allows authenticated users to read other tenants' investigation runs by supplying their run_id. items.summary: ToDesktop Builder before 0.36.1 contains a path traversal vulnerability in the todesktop-fs custom protocol handler that allows attackers to escape the bundled files directory using ../ sequences. items.summary: A vulnerability has been found in KeudellCoding User Location Map up to 1.2.5. items.summary: In mcp-server-fetch from 2026.10.10 and before 2026.11.11, the check that blocks requests to non-public addresses treats IPv6 site-local addresses (fec0::/10) as public. items.summary: In mcp-server-git before 2026.10.28, the --repository restriction can be bypassed through a nested directory that contains a .git file with a gitdir pointer to a repository outside the allowed path. items.title: CVE-2026-133632: In astro-airflow-mcp 0.5.0 through 0.9.1, the af CLI and the MCP server send telemetry from a Python subprocess that can import modules from the current working directory. If a use
items.summary: In astro-airflow-mcp 0.5.0 through 0.9.1, the af CLI and the MCP server send telemetry from a Python subprocess that can import modules from the current working directory. If a user runs an af command or an MCP tool call from inside a project that contains an attacker-supplied json.py, that file runs with the user's privileges. Users who only run the tool in projects they trust are not affected. Fixed in 0.9.2; in earlier versions, setting AF_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1 prevents it.

items.title: CVE-2026-132779: When NGINX Plus or NGINX Open Source is configured to use TLS 1.3 early data using the ssl_early_data on directive, an attacker can use a specially crafted TLS 1.3 connection to dr
items.summary: When NGINX Plus or NGINX Open Source is configured to use TLS 1.3 early data using the ssl_early_data on directive, an attacker can use a specially crafted TLS 1.3 connection to drive an NGINX worker into a tight loop in which it repeatedly retries the same send without ever making progress. The worker continues accepting new connections and handling existing ones, but one CPU core is pinned at 100%. Impact: System performance can degrade until the NGINX worker process is either forced to restart or is manually restarted. This vulnerability may allow an unauthenticated attacker to cause a degradation of service that can lead to a denial-of-service (DoS) on the NGINX system. There is no control plane exposure; this is a data plane issue only. Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

items.title: CVE-2026-129975: A flaw was found in gpgme. When processing crafted input, an early return following memory reallocation can leave internal buffer pointers referencing previously freed memory, resu
items.summary: A flaw was found in gpgme. When processing crafted input, an early return following memory reallocation can leave internal buffer pointers referencing previously freed memory, resulting in a double-free condition during cleanup. A remote attacker could exploit this vulnerability to corrupt process memory, potentially leading to arbitrary code execution or a Denial of Service (DoS) crash.

items.summary: Dell Enterprise Sonic Distribution, versions prior to 4.6.1, contains an Argument Injection vulnerability. A low privileged remote attacker could potentially exploit this vulnerability, leading to arbitrary command execution and unauthorized access to filesystem resources.

items.title: CVE-2026-107784: On Windows, the tarfile "tar" and "data" extraction filters did not reject member names or link targets that have a drive but no root, such as "C:foo". When extracting to a relativ
items.summary: On Windows, the tarfile "tar" and "data" extraction filters did not reject member names or link targets that have a drive but no root, such as "C:foo". When extracting to a relative destination, such a member was written to the current working directory of that drive instead of the destination, and a symbolic link with such a target pointed outside the destination. The filters now refuse these member names and link targets with AbsolutePathError and AbsoluteLinkError.

items.title: Cisco Expressway Series Remote Code Execution Vulnerability
items.summary: A vulnerability in the database service feature of Cisco Expressway Series could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker with network access to a Cisco Expressway device to execute arbitrary operating system commands as root . This vulnerability is due to the use of persistent cookies. Additionally, there is insufficient validation of client certificates when the TLS Verify Mode is set to Enabled for clustering, which means that client certificates are not validated. An attacker with possession of the cookies could exploit this vulnerability by connecting to the database service and invoking specific remote procedure call (RPC) commands. A successful exploit could allow the attacker to execute arbitrary commands as root on the underlying operating system of an affected device. Note: Cisco Expressway Series refers to Cisco Expressway Core (Expressway-C) devices and Cisco Expressway Edge (Expressway-E) devices. Cisco has released software updates that address this vulnerability. There are no workarounds that address this vulnerability. This advisory is available at the following link: https://sec.cloudapps.cisco.com/security/center/content/CiscoSecurityAdvisory/cisco-sa-vcs-static-

When wavelet denoising threshold or chromatic aberration correction is enabled, the destimage buffer is sized from halved iwidth/iheight but indexed at full width, causing writes of file-derived pixel values beyond the allocation and crashes.

items.summary: PdfPig through 0.1.16 contains an uncontrolled recursion vulnerability that allows attackers to crash applications by supplying crafted PDF documents with self-referencing AcroForm /Kids or deeply nested marked content. items.summary: Softaculous Virtualizor before 3.2.9 contains an SQL injection vulnerability in enduser/auth_callback.php that allows unauthenticated attackers to bypass authentication via OAuth-returned email addresses. items.summary: ZITADEL 4.19.5 before 4.20.3 contains a host header injection vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to redirect notification links by placing a trusted host in the userinfo portion of the x-zitadel-public-host header. items.summary: Formance Ledger 2.2.0-beta.3 before 2.4.18 contains an SQL injection vulnerability that allows remote API callers to execute SQL by supplying unvalidated account expand values. items.summary: CISO Assistant before 4.2.3 contains a denial of service vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to block all logins by exhausting a shared rate limit keyed on the frontend server IP. items.summary: Umbraco CMS 17.4.0 before 17.8.2 and 18.0.0 before 18.3.2 contains an information disclosure vulnerability because MemberValueSetBuilder.GetValueSets writes sensitive member properties into the Examine members index. items.summary: LibRaw 0.22.0 through 0.22.3 contains a heap out-of-bounds read vulnerability in HuffTable::len() because parse_dht() stores Huffman DC symbols without validating them as difference categories. items.summary: Windmill 1.664.0 before 1.819.0 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows any workspace member to mint resume signatures for suspended jobs via create_job_signature, get_resume_urls and get_wac_approval_urls handlers. items.summary: Interstellar before 6.3.0 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to reach internal services by enabling allow_loopback_ips and allow_private_ips in wisp-js at startup. items.summary: PodFetch 5.2.0 before 5.3.1 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the Audiobookshelf-compatible POST /api/podcasts endpoint that allows authenticated low-privilege users to add podcasts by bypassing role and USER_PODCAST_LIMIT checks. items.summary: Windmill 1.607.0 before 1.819.0 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows workspace members to resume or cancel suspended flows in other workspaces by abusing the jobs_u/resume and jobs_u/cancel endpoints. items.title: CVE-2026-93585: An improper authorization vulnerability in the EasyVistas EV Reach Client Agent allows authenticated users with low privileges to execute arbitrary commands on a remote Windows end
items.summary: An improper authorization vulnerability in the EasyVistas EV Reach Client Agent allows authenticated users with low privileges to execute arbitrary commands on a remote Windows endpoint with LocalSystem privileges. The affected agent service does not sufficiently enforce authorization restrictions for certain privileged remote management operations. Under specific conditions, the agent fails to apply the intended user impersonation mechanism and executes user-supplied commands within the security context of the agent service, which runs as NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM. As a result, an authenticated attacker may bypass the intended privilege restrictions and execute arbitrary commands with the highest user-mode privileges on an affected Windows system. Successful exploitation may lead to complete compromise of the affected endpoint, including unauthorized access to sensitive information, modification of system configurations, installation of malicious software, or disruption of system availability. The vulnerability does not require administrative credentials or user interaction after successful authentication.

items.title: CVE-2026-86312: Under some configurations a request to the ping endpoint could carry out more than a simple health check. In deployments that rely on Solr's rule-based authorization, a client gran
items.summary: Under some configurations a request to the ping endpoint could carry out more than a simple health check. In deployments that rely on Solr's rule-based authorization, a client granted only the low-privilege health permission could thereby trigger behavior that should require higher privileges; where the shipped security.json template leaves the health permission unauthenticated, no credentials are required at all. This issue affects Apache Solr from 9.0.0 through the releases preceding the fixed versions. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 9.11.0 or 10.1.0, which resolve the issue. You are affected if you run an affected version and allow the /admin/ping endpoint to be reached with only the health permission. This includes the default sample security configuration installed by the bin/solr CLI, where that endpoint is unauthenticated. Users who cannot upgrade immediately should restrict access to the /admin/ping endpoint in their authorization configuration — for example by requiring a trusted role for that path — and ensure Solr is not reachable from untrusted clients or networks, as recommended for all Solr deployments.

items.title: CVE-2026-53672: A bug related to the Zookeeper HTTP endpoints in Apache Solr allows an authenticated attacker with zk-read permission to read /security.json, bypassing the security-read authorizat
items.summary: A bug related to the Zookeeper HTTP endpoints in Apache Solr allows an authenticated attacker with zk-read permission to read /security.json, bypassing the security-read authorization check. This may cause unauthorized read of credential hashes and authorization configuration. For this attack to be successful, the following must be true * The system is secured with Solr's Basic Auth plugin * The attacker has gained direct network access to the Solr cluster * The attacker has obtained credentials for a user account with zk-read permission (which is recommended assigned to trusted admins only) Users are recommended to upgrade to 9.11.0, 10.1.0 or a newer release. Users who cannot upgrade immediately are recommended to assign the zk-read permission only to users who they entrust reading security.json.

items.title: CVE-2026-125651: Cleartext storage in encrypted parquet file vulnerability in Apache Arrow Rust (`parquet` crate), from version 55.0.0 through to 57.3.2, 58.4.1, 59.3.2 and 60.1.0. When writing
items.summary: Cleartext storage in encrypted parquet file vulnerability in Apache Arrow Rust (`parquet` crate), from version 55.0.0 through to 57.3.2, 58.4.1, 59.3.2 and 60.1.0. When writing an encrypted parquet file with a column with bloom filters, the header and bitsets of the bloom filter are written in plaintext in the final parquet. Users are recommended to upgrade to versions 57.3.3, 58.4.2, 59.3.3 or 60.2.0 which fix the issue by raising an error when trying to write encrypted parquet files with bloom filters enabled, preventing such files from being written out. Existing encrypted parquet files written with bloom filters are still vulnerable, and it is recommended to rewrite those files with bloom filters disabled if possible.

items.title: CVE-2026-135055: A flaw was found in the GLib DMA-BUF path of WebKitGTK. The UIProcess trusted fds.size() as the DMA-BUF plane count when handling AcceleratedBackingStore::DidCreateDMABufBuffer and
items.summary: A flaw was found in the GLib DMA-BUF path of WebKitGTK. The UIProcess trusted fds.size() as the DMA-BUF plane count when handling AcceleratedBackingStore::DidCreateDMABufBuffer and copied offsets and strides without verifying that those vectors had the same length. A compromised WebProcess can send mismatched vector lengths, causing an out-of-bounds read in the privileged UIProcess. This can disclose UIProcess memory and crash the UIProcess, and may be used as part of a Web Content sandbox-escape chain.

items.title: CVE-2026-59340: PagePdfDocumentReader and ParagraphPdfDocumentReader are vulnerable to a denial of service when processing untrusted PDF input. The underlying text extraction logic reconstruct
items.summary: PagePdfDocumentReader and ParagraphPdfDocumentReader are vulnerable to a denial of service when processing untrusted PDF input. The underlying text extraction logic reconstructs layout from a PDF's glyph positions and limits how much memory can be allocated for any single computed gap, but does not limit the cumulative allocation across an entire page. A specially crafted PDF can exploit this to force excessive memory allocation during processing, resulting in OutOfMemoryError. Depending on JVM configuration, this can cause request failures with degraded service under repeated exploitation, or immediate JVM termination when ExitOnOutOfMemoryError options are used. Any application that processes PDFs from untrusted sources (document upload, email attachment processing, RAG ingestion, web crawling) using either affected reader is impacted.

items.title: CVE-2026-59442: TypesenseFilterExpressionConverter does not correctly translate grouped (parenthesized) filter expressions into the Typesense filter syntax. As a result, the filter sent to Type
items.summary: TypesenseFilterExpressionConverter does not correctly translate grouped (parenthesized) filter expressions into the Typesense filter syntax. As a result, the filter sent to Typesense can have a different meaning than the one the application defined, and some conditions may not be applied as intended. An application is affected if it uses the Typesense vector store with filter expressions that contain groups and relies on them to restrict results, for example to enforce tenant isolation or access control. In that case, a remote user may be able to retrieve documents they should not have access to, and the same filter used for a delete operation may remove documents outside the intended scope.

items.title: CVE-2026-133646: Synchronet BBS, in versions 3.20b to 3.21e, contains an out-of-bounds write vulnerability in the answer() function when processing the terminal attribute of the SSH service. The ca
items.summary: Synchronet BBS, in versions 3.20b to 3.21e, contains an out-of-bounds write vulnerability in the answer() function when processing the terminal attribute of the SSH service. The call to cryptGetAttributeString() does not limit the copy to the size of the destination buffer, of which 41 bytes are used. An unauthenticated remote client can send a TERM value of up to 64 bytes and overwrite adjacent fields of the session object. If the SSH service is enabled, this tampering can cause connection threads to be blocked for an extended period, even after the client has disconnected. By exhausting the available sockets, the attacker can prevent new connections and cause a denial of service requiring the software to be restarted.

items.title: CVE-2026-123886: Spring Data Elasticsearch replaces positional placeholders in string-based @Query methods with the method arguments before it evaluates SpEL expressions in the resulting query stri
items.summary: Spring Data Elasticsearch replaces positional placeholders in string-based @Query methods with the method arguments before it evaluates SpEL expressions in the resulting query string. As a result, an argument that contains a SpEL expression is evaluated as part of the query, even if the declared query does not use SpEL. An application is affected if it passes untrusted input as an argument to a repository query method that declares a @Query with positional placeholders. In that case, a remote attacker can execute arbitrary code in the application, and repeated requests can exhaust memory through the unbounded expression cache.

The vulnerability occurs because libdigidocpp does not properly validate the Extended Key Usage (EKU) extension of certificates used to sign OCSP responses. Specifically, it fails to verify that the certificate contains the id-kp-OCSPSigning EKU, which identifies certificates authorised to sign OCSP responses. This issue affects libdigidocpp: from 3.10.0 before 4.5.2; DigiDoc4: from 4.0.0 before 4.11.2; DigiDoc: from 3.0.0 before 3.2.0; DigiDoc: from 3.0.1 before 3.2.0.

items.title: VirtualBox Process Hardening on Windows 2026 Edition: What’s a Single Bit Between Friends?
items.summary: Back in 2017 I did some research into Oracle VirtualBox on Windows. Specifically I focussed on their mechanism to protect their VM processes from the user on the host. The protection was to gate who could open the kernel driver, which might allow for privilege escalation due to the way it was designed. At the time I found 3 ways of bypassing the protection, with an additional issue in COM’s runtime I reported in 2020. These issues were all written up in this post. Fast forward to 2026 and I decided to look at VirtualBox again to see if much had changed. This time I found 3 new bypasses for protected processes, with an additional bug which was a broken fix for the 2020 bypass breaking due to changes in Windows.

items.summary: A security vulnerability has been detected in xuxueli xxl-job 3.5.0/3.5.1-SNAPSHOT. items.summary: Assimp through 6.0.6 contains an infinite loop vulnerability in ColladaParser::ReadPrimitives that allows attackers to exhaust memory via non-numeric index values. Attackers can supply a crafted Collada file whose index list contains a non-digit character, causing endless zero-index appends until the importing process crashes.

items.summary: Assimp through 6.0.6 contains an out-of-bounds read vulnerability in glTFImporter::ImportMeshes that uses NORMAL and TEXCOORD accessors without comparing their counts to the POSITION vertex count. Attackers can supply a crafted glTF 1.0 file with shorter normal or texture coordinate arrays to trigger heap out-of-bounds reads and writes that crash the importing application.

items.summary: Assimp through 6.0.6 contains an invalid pointer dereference vulnerability in glTFImporter::ImportEmbeddedTextures that derives the texture format hint without checking the strchr result. Attackers can supply a crafted glTF 1.0 file with an embedded image mime type lacking a slash to crash the importing application.

items.summary: Assimp through 6.0.6 contains a use of uninitialized resource vulnerability in glTFImporter::ImportMeshes that builds TRIANGLE_STRIP and TRIANGLE_FAN faces from unfilled faces. Attackers can supply a crafted glTF 1.0 file whose strip or fan primitives trigger out-of-bounds reads or null pointer dereferences, crashing the importing application.
